# Reports API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

Plain-dictionary reports of a calibrated model and of a run. Guide: [Reports](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/reports/index.md).

## applied_parameters_report

```python
applied_parameters_report(model: Model, result: CalibrationResult | Mapping[str, float], problem: CalibrationProblem | None = None, sample: ParameterSample | None = None, confidence_level: float | None = None) -> AppliedParametersReport
```

Report every parameter of a calibrated model, and the values of its kind.

Each entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted ones. The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind (`ModelStructure.report_sections`); an aggregate model adds `initial_amounts` and `category_splits`.

Parameters that are not a single number, such as a formula or a series, are omitted: they are inputs rather than fitted values. `factor` and `noise` parameters have no place in the model, so they are reported from `problem` when it is given.

`initial_amounts` gives each bin and each overridden compartment of an aggregate model its `amount` the engine builds and the `unit` of its bin, so bins of different units are reported side by side; no row is a share of a total. A bin left uncalibrated keeps a `None` amount as its "needs calibration" marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments. `category_splits` gives each category its `fraction` of the group it splits, and that `group`: the categories a conditional stratification is conditioned on, empty when it splits every bin.

With a `sample` each entry gains an `interval` holding the weighted statistics of its draws (`ParameterSample.summary`). Every entry is in the unit it was calibrated in: a parameter in its own, an amount in the unit of its bin, and a category split as a fraction of its group.

Parameters:

| Name               | Type                 | Description                            | Default                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`            | `Model`              | The model carrying the applied values. | *required*                                                                                  |
| `result`           | \`CalibrationResult  | Mapping\`                              | The calibration result, or a mapping of parameter id to value such as one draw of a sample. |
| `problem`          | \`CalibrationProblem | None\`                                 | The problem the result came from, used to report factor and noise parameters.               |
| `sample`           | \`ParameterSample    | None\`                                 | Draws of the parameters, such as the sample of an uncertainty method.                       |
| `confidence_level` | \`float              | None\`                                 | Confidence level of the intervals; required with a sample.                                  |

Returns:

| Type                      | Description                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AppliedParametersReport` | Key parameters and the sections of the kind (initial_amounts and category_splits for an aggregate model), preceded by confidence_level when there is one. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If a sample is given without a confidence level. |

Source code in `commol/api/reporting.py`

```python
def applied_parameters_report(
    model: Model,
    result: CalibrationResult | Mapping[str, float],
    problem: CalibrationProblem | None = None,
    sample: ParameterSample | None = None,
    confidence_level: float | None = None,
) -> AppliedParametersReport:
    """
    Report every parameter of a calibrated model, and the values of its kind.

    Each entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set
    it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted ones.
    The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind
    (`ModelStructure.report_sections`); an aggregate model adds
    ``initial_amounts`` and ``category_splits``.

    Parameters that are not a single number, such as a formula or a
    series, are omitted: they are inputs rather than fitted values.
    ``factor`` and ``noise`` parameters have no place in the model, so they are
    reported from `problem` when it is given.

    ``initial_amounts`` gives each bin and each overridden compartment of an
    aggregate model its ``amount`` the engine builds and the ``unit`` of its
    bin, so bins of different units are reported side by side; no row is a
    share of a total. A bin left uncalibrated keeps a ``None`` amount as its
    "needs calibration" marker even when overrides touch some of its
    compartments. ``category_splits`` gives each category its ``fraction`` of
    the group it splits, and that ``group``: the categories a conditional
    stratification is conditioned on, empty when it splits every bin.

    With a `sample` each entry gains an ``interval`` holding the weighted
    statistics of its draws (`ParameterSample.summary`). Every entry is in
    the unit it was calibrated in: a parameter in its own, an amount in the
    unit of its bin, and a category split as a fraction of its group.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : Model
        The model carrying the applied values.
    result : CalibrationResult | Mapping
        The calibration result, or a mapping of parameter id to value such as
        one draw of a sample.
    problem : CalibrationProblem | None, optional
        The problem the result came from, used to report factor and noise
        parameters.
    sample : ParameterSample | None, optional
        Draws of the parameters, such as the sample of an uncertainty method.
    confidence_level : float | None, optional
        Confidence level of the intervals; required with a sample.

    Returns
    -------
    AppliedParametersReport
        Key ``parameters`` and the sections of the kind (``initial_amounts``
        and ``category_splits`` for an aggregate model), preceded by
        ``confidence_level`` when there is one.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a sample is given without a confidence level.
    """
    calibrated = calibrated_values(result)
    parameter_statistics = _sample_statistics(sample, confidence_level)
    calibrated_ids = set(calibrated)

    parameters: dict[str, ParameterEntry] = {
        parameter.id: _parameter_entry(
            parameter.id, parameter.value, calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics
        )
        for parameter in model.parameters
        if isinstance(parameter.value, (int, float))
    }
    for observation_id in _observation_parameter_ids(problem):
        if observation_id in calibrated:
            parameters[observation_id] = _parameter_entry(
                observation_id,
                calibrated[observation_id],
                calibrated_ids,
                parameter_statistics,
            )

    report: dict[str, object] = {}
    # `confidence_level` leads the report, so it is written first.
    if confidence_level is not None:
        report["confidence_level"] = confidence_level
    report["parameters"] = parameters
    report.update(
        model.structure.report_sections(model, calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics)
    )
    return cast(AppliedParametersReport, report)
```

## simulation_report

```python
simulation_report(simulation: Simulation, results: SimulationResults, at: Sequence[float], window: float, num_windows: int, observed_data: Iterable[ObservedDataPoint] = (), accumulators: Iterable[str] = (), ensemble_runs: Sequence[SimulationResults] | Predictive | None = None, confidence_level: float | None = None, prediction_intervals: PredictionIntervals | None = None) -> SimulationReport
```

Report the observed data, compartment series and accumulators of a run.

The three blocks share one window axis, so the observed values, the windowed accumulator increments and the sampled series can be read against each other. With `ensemble_runs` every leaf becomes a `{mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max}` block computed across members, and the layout is otherwise unchanged.

Callers add whatever envelope they need around these blocks, such as a run label, axis labels or domain-specific summary figures.

Parameters:

| Name                   | Type                          | Description                                                      | Default                                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `simulation`           | `Simulation`                  | The simulation the results came from.                            | *required*                                                                                    |
| `results`              | `SimulationResults`           | Results of a run, with their positions.                          | *required*                                                                                    |
| `at`                   | `Sequence[float]`             | Positions the series and cumulative accumulators are sampled at. | *required*                                                                                    |
| `window`               | `float`                       | Length of one window on the axis.                                | *required*                                                                                    |
| `num_windows`          | `int`                         | Number of windows on the observed and windowed axes.             | *required*                                                                                    |
| `observed_data`        | `Iterable[ObservedDataPoint]` | The calibration targets to report alongside the run.             | `()`                                                                                          |
| `accumulators`         | `Iterable[str]`               | Accumulator ids to report.                                       | `()`                                                                                          |
| `ensemble_runs`        | \`Sequence[SimulationResults] | Predictive                                                       | None\`                                                                                        |
| `confidence_level`     | \`float                       | None\`                                                           | Confidence level of the reported intervals.                                                   |
| `prediction_intervals` | \`PredictionIntervals         | None\`                                                           | Prediction intervals of a conformal method (ConformalResult.intervals), reported as they are. |

Returns:

| Type               | Description                                                                            |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SimulationReport` | Keys observed, series and accumulators, then prediction_intervals when they are given. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If the results have no value at a position the report reads. |

Source code in `commol/api/reporting.py`

```python
def simulation_report(
    simulation: Simulation,
    results: SimulationResults,
    at: Sequence[float],
    window: float,
    num_windows: int,
    observed_data: Iterable[ObservedDataPoint] = (),
    accumulators: Iterable[str] = (),
    ensemble_runs: "Sequence[SimulationResults] | Predictive | None" = None,
    confidence_level: float | None = None,
    prediction_intervals: PredictionIntervals | None = None,
) -> SimulationReport:
    """
    Report the observed data, compartment series and accumulators of a run.

    The three blocks share one window axis, so the observed values, the
    windowed accumulator increments and the sampled series can be read against
    each other. With `ensemble_runs` every leaf becomes a
    ``{mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max}`` block computed across
    members, and the layout is otherwise unchanged.

    Callers add whatever envelope they need around these blocks, such as a run
    label, axis labels or domain-specific summary figures.

    Parameters
    ----------
    simulation : Simulation
        The simulation the results came from.
    results : SimulationResults
        Results of a run, with their positions.
    at : Sequence[float]
        Positions the series and cumulative accumulators are sampled at.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    num_windows : int
        Number of windows on the observed and windowed axes.
    observed_data : Iterable[ObservedDataPoint], optional
        The calibration targets to report alongside the run.
    accumulators : Iterable[str], optional
        Accumulator ids to report.
    ensemble_runs : Sequence[SimulationResults] | Predictive | None, optional
        One results mapping per member, such as the replicates of a stochastic
        engine, or a `Predictive`, whose draws carry their weights.
    confidence_level : float | None, optional
        Confidence level of the reported intervals.
    prediction_intervals : PredictionIntervals | None, optional
        Prediction intervals of a conformal method
        (``ConformalResult.intervals``), reported as they are.

    Returns
    -------
    SimulationReport
        Keys ``observed``, ``series`` and ``accumulators``, then
        ``prediction_intervals`` when they are given.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the results have no value at a position the report reads.
    """
    accumulator_ids = list(accumulators)
    report: SimulationReport = {
        "observed": observed_report(observed_data, window, num_windows),
        "series": series_report(
            simulation,
            results,
            at,
            accumulator_ids,
            ensemble_runs,
            confidence_level,
        ),
        "accumulators": accumulators_report(
            simulation,
            results,
            accumulator_ids,
            at,
            window,
            num_windows,
            ensemble_runs,
            confidence_level,
        ),
    }
    if prediction_intervals is not None:
        report["prediction_intervals"] = cast(
            "PredictionIntervalsReport", prediction_intervals.model_dump()
        )
    return report
```

Source code in `commol/api/reporting.py`

```python
def identifiability_report(report: IdentifiabilityReport) -> IdentifiabilityReportData:
    """
    Report the identifiability of each parameter as plain data.

    Parameters
    ----------
    report : IdentifiabilityReport
        The result of ``Calibrator.identifiability``, or of
        `IdentifiabilityReport.merge`.

    Returns
    -------
    IdentifiabilityReportData
        ``parameters``: each parameter, in problem order, with its structural
        and practical verdicts; ``sections``: the evidence of each method that
        ran.
    """
    parameters: dict[str, VerdictsEntry] = {}
    for name in report.parameters:
        verdicts = report.verdicts[name]
        structural = verdicts.structural
        practical = verdicts.practical
        parameters[name] = {
            "structural": None
            if structural is None
            else {
                "verdict": structural.verdict,
                "reasons": list(structural.reasons),
                "combinations": list(structural.combinations),
            },
            "practical": None
            if practical is None
            else {"verdict": practical.verdict, "reasons": list(practical.reasons)},
        }
    sections: dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]] = {
        "structural": [section.model_dump() for section in report.structural],
        "collinearity": [section.model_dump() for section in report.collinearity],
        "sample": [section.model_dump() for section in report.sample],
        "starts": [section.model_dump() for section in report.starts],
    }
    return {"parameters": parameters, "sections": sections}
```

# Sensitivity API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

The sensitivity analysis, what it varies, the quantities of interest it reads from each run, and the base of its methods. Guide: [Sensitivity analysis](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/index.md).

## SensitivityAnalysis

The forward questions of a model: how uncertainty in its inputs moves its outputs, and which inputs matter most.

A calibration asks which inputs fit the data; an analysis needs no data. It holds the simulation, what varies (`InputSpace`), the replicates of a stochastic engine and the seed of every random number, and every method of one analysis reads the same inputs. The forward model is built in Rust once, when the analysis is created: the values of the inputs reach the engine as a calibration writes them.

Source code in `commol/api/sensitivity.py`

```python
class SensitivityAnalysis:
    """
    The forward questions of a model: how uncertainty in its inputs moves its
    outputs, and which inputs matter most.

    A calibration asks which inputs fit the data; an analysis needs no data.
    It holds the simulation, what varies (`InputSpace`), the replicates of a
    stochastic engine and the seed of every random number, and every method
    of one analysis reads the same inputs. The forward model is built in Rust
    once, when the analysis is created: the values of the inputs reach the
    engine as a calibration writes them.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        simulation: Simulation,
        inputs: InputSpace,
        *,
        replicates: int | None = None,
        seed: int | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Build the analysis of `inputs` on `simulation`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        simulation : Simulation
            The model to analyse.
        inputs : InputSpace
            What varies.
        replicates : int | None, optional
            For a stochastic engine, required, at least 1: how many replicates
            each point runs. A point of the design of PRCC, Morris, Sobol or
            polynomial chaos holds the mean of its replicates, on the same
            seeds at every point; a propagation keeps every replicate, each
            with a seed of its own. A deterministic engine does not use it, so
            the same analysis runs on either engine.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of the designs and the replicates. Required with a
            stochastic engine; otherwise None draws one from the operating
            system, which the analysis logs.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an input is not a value of the model, the replicates or the
            seed do not fit the engine, `replicates` is below 1, or the seed
            is not a whole number from 0 to ``2**64 - 1``.
        """
        engine_type = simulation.model_definition.engine.type
        stochastic = commol_rs.engine.EngineType(engine_type).is_stochastic
        if replicates is not None and replicates < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"replicates is at least 1, got {replicates}")
        if stochastic and replicates is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set replicates, how many "
                "replicates each point of a design runs."
            )
        if stochastic and seed is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set seed, so the "
                "replicates and the analysis are reproducible."
            )
        self.simulation: Simulation = simulation
        self.inputs: InputSpace = inputs
        self.replicates: int | None = replicates
        if seed is not None:
            check_seed(seed)
        self._seed: int | None = seed
        check_values(
            simulation.model_definition,
            simulation.engine,
            inputs.parameters,
            inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
        )
        self._rust: "ForwardAnalysisProtocol" = commol_rs.inference.ForwardAnalysis(
            simulation.engine,
            engine_state.rust_parameters(inputs.parameters),
            distributions=inputs.rust_distributions(),
            sample=None if inputs.sample is None else inputs.sample.rust_sample,
            initial_condition_remainder=inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
            replicates=replicates if stochastic else None,
            seed=self.seed,
        )

    @property
    def rust_analysis(self) -> "ForwardAnalysisProtocol":
        """
        The forward analysis built in Rust, for the runners of methods.

        Returns
        -------
        ForwardAnalysisProtocol
            The forward model and the inputs every method reads.
        """
        return self._rust

    def rust_predictive(
        self, sample: ParameterSample, positions: list[float]
    ) -> "PredictiveProtocol":
        """
        The run of every draw of `sample` at `positions`, for a `Predictive`:
        each replicate of a stochastic engine has a seed of its own, derived
        from the seed of the analysis, as in a propagation.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws, in the order of the inputs.
        positions : list[float]
            Positions to report at, sorted and unique.

        Returns
        -------
        PredictiveProtocol
            The runs, computed in Rust.
        """
        return self._rust.predictive(sample.rust_sample, positions)

    def rust_observation_draws(
        self,
        sample: ParameterSample,
        observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint],
        noise: ObservationNoise,
    ) -> "ObservationDrawsProtocol":
        """
        Every draw's value of `observed_data`, for a `Predictive`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws, in the order of the inputs.
        observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint]
            The observations.
        noise : NoNoise | ResidualNoise | DistributionNoise
            The observation noise; only ``NoNoise()``.

        Returns
        -------
        ObservationDrawsProtocol
            The draws, computed in Rust.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the noise is not ``NoNoise()``: residual noise needs the
            residuals of a fit, distribution noise the observation models of a
            problem, and an analysis has neither.
        """
        if not isinstance(noise, NoNoise):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{type(noise).__name__} needs a calibration: residual noise reads "
                "the residuals of a fit and distribution noise the observation "
                "models of a problem, and a sensitivity analysis has no data. Read "
                "the observations with NoNoise()."
            )
        return self._rust.observation_draws(
            sample.rust_sample, engine_state.rust_observed_data(observed_data)
        )

    def rust_log_score(
        self,
        sample: ParameterSample,  # noqa: ARG002
        observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint],  # noqa: ARG002
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Refuse the log score, which `commol.scores.log_score` asks for.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws.
        observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint]
            The observations.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            Always: the log score reads the observation models of a problem,
            and an analysis has no data.
        """
        raise ValueError(
            "The log score needs the observation models of a calibration problem, "
            "and a sensitivity analysis has no data."
        )

    @property
    def seed(self) -> int:
        """
        The seed of the analysis' random numbers.

        Returns
        -------
        int
            The seed given, or a seed drawn from the operating system once
            per analysis and logged.
        """
        if self._seed is not None:
            return self._seed
        if not hasattr(self, "_drawn_seed"):
            self._drawn_seed = draw_seed()
            logger.info(
                "No seed set; drew the seed %d, which repeats this analysis.",
                self._drawn_seed,
            )
        return self._drawn_seed

    def run(self, method: SensitivityMethod[ResultT]) -> ResultT:
        """
        Run a sensitivity method on the inputs of this analysis.

        Parameters
        ----------
        method : SensitivityMethod[ResultT]
            The configuration of the method; its type sets the result type.

        Returns
        -------
        ResultT
            The method's result.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If `method` is not a sensitivity method; the message names its
            entry point.
        ValueError
            If the method does not take these inputs, such as a method of
            independent inputs on inputs from a sample.
        """
        return run_method(self, method, SensitivityMethod)
```

Source code in `commol/api/sensitivity.py`

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    simulation: Simulation,
    inputs: InputSpace,
    *,
    replicates: int | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
):
    """
    Build the analysis of `inputs` on `simulation`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    simulation : Simulation
        The model to analyse.
    inputs : InputSpace
        What varies.
    replicates : int | None, optional
        For a stochastic engine, required, at least 1: how many replicates
        each point runs. A point of the design of PRCC, Morris, Sobol or
        polynomial chaos holds the mean of its replicates, on the same
        seeds at every point; a propagation keeps every replicate, each
        with a seed of its own. A deterministic engine does not use it, so
        the same analysis runs on either engine.
    seed : int | None, optional
        The seed of the designs and the replicates. Required with a
        stochastic engine; otherwise None draws one from the operating
        system, which the analysis logs.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an input is not a value of the model, the replicates or the
        seed do not fit the engine, `replicates` is below 1, or the seed
        is not a whole number from 0 to ``2**64 - 1``.
    """
    engine_type = simulation.model_definition.engine.type
    stochastic = commol_rs.engine.EngineType(engine_type).is_stochastic
    if replicates is not None and replicates < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"replicates is at least 1, got {replicates}")
    if stochastic and replicates is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set replicates, how many "
            "replicates each point of a design runs."
        )
    if stochastic and seed is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set seed, so the "
            "replicates and the analysis are reproducible."
        )
    self.simulation: Simulation = simulation
    self.inputs: InputSpace = inputs
    self.replicates: int | None = replicates
    if seed is not None:
        check_seed(seed)
    self._seed: int | None = seed
    check_values(
        simulation.model_definition,
        simulation.engine,
        inputs.parameters,
        inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
    )
    self._rust: "ForwardAnalysisProtocol" = commol_rs.inference.ForwardAnalysis(
        simulation.engine,
        engine_state.rust_parameters(inputs.parameters),
        distributions=inputs.rust_distributions(),
        sample=None if inputs.sample is None else inputs.sample.rust_sample,
        initial_condition_remainder=inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
        replicates=replicates if stochastic else None,
        seed=self.seed,
    )
```

Source code in `commol/api/sensitivity.py`

```python
def rust_observation_draws(
    self,
    sample: ParameterSample,
    observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint],
    noise: ObservationNoise,
) -> "ObservationDrawsProtocol":
    """
    Every draw's value of `observed_data`, for a `Predictive`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    sample : ParameterSample
        The draws, in the order of the inputs.
    observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint]
        The observations.
    noise : NoNoise | ResidualNoise | DistributionNoise
        The observation noise; only ``NoNoise()``.

    Returns
    -------
    ObservationDrawsProtocol
        The draws, computed in Rust.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the noise is not ``NoNoise()``: residual noise needs the
        residuals of a fit, distribution noise the observation models of a
        problem, and an analysis has neither.
    """
    if not isinstance(noise, NoNoise):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(noise).__name__} needs a calibration: residual noise reads "
            "the residuals of a fit and distribution noise the observation "
            "models of a problem, and a sensitivity analysis has no data. Read "
            "the observations with NoNoise()."
        )
    return self._rust.observation_draws(
        sample.rust_sample, engine_state.rust_observed_data(observed_data)
    )
```

## InputSpace

Bases: `BaseModel`

What a sensitivity analysis varies.

Each input is a `CalibrationParameter`, a model parameter or an initial condition with its bounds, as a calibration sets it. The inputs follow independent distributions, one per input, truncated to its bounds, or are the draws of a sample, with their weights; the inputs of a sample may depend on each other, so only the methods that allow it take one. Build it with `independent`, `uniform_on_bounds` or `from_sample`.

Attributes:

| Name                          | Type                         | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parameters`                  | `list[CalibrationParameter]` | The inputs, in order. A factor or a noise parameter is not an input: both belong to observations, and an analysis has none. |
| `distributions`               | \`dict[str, Distribution]    | None\`                                                                                                                      |
| `sample`                      | \`ParameterSample            | None\`                                                                                                                      |
| `initial_condition_remainder` | \`str                        | None\`                                                                                                                      |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python
class InputSpace(BaseModel):
    """
    What a sensitivity analysis varies.

    Each input is a `CalibrationParameter`, a model parameter or an initial
    condition with its bounds, as a calibration sets it. The inputs follow
    independent distributions, one per input, truncated to its bounds, or
    are the draws of a sample, with their weights; the inputs of a sample may
    depend on each other, so only the methods that allow it take one. Build
    it with `independent`, `uniform_on_bounds` or `from_sample`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    parameters : list[CalibrationParameter]
        The inputs, in order. A factor or a noise parameter is not an input:
        both belong to observations, and an analysis has none.
    distributions : dict[str, Distribution] | None
        The distribution of each input, for independent inputs.
    sample : ParameterSample | None
        The draws of the inputs, for inputs from a sample.
    initial_condition_remainder : str | None
        The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions leave
        of the sum the model states, as in a calibration problem.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    parameters: list[CalibrationParameter] = Field(
        min_length=1, description="The inputs, in order."
    )
    distributions: dict[str, Distribution] | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The distribution of each independent input."
    )
    sample: ParameterSample | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The draws of inputs from a sample."
    )
    initial_condition_remainder: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions leave.",
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_inputs(self) -> Self:
        """Check the inputs against the distributions or the sample."""
        ids = [parameter.id for parameter in self.parameters]
        repeated = sorted({i for i in ids if ids.count(i) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise ValueError(f"Inputs repeat the ids {repeated}.")
        observed = {
            CalibrationParameterType.FACTOR: (
                "a factor, which multiplies an observation"
            ),
            CalibrationParameterType.NOISE: (
                "a noise parameter, which belongs to an observation model"
            ),
        }
        for parameter in self.parameters:
            what = observed.get(CalibrationParameterType(parameter.parameter_type))
            if what is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"'{parameter.id}' is {what}; a sensitivity analysis has no "
                    "observations."
                )
        if (self.distributions is None) == (self.sample is None):
            raise ValueError("Give distributions or a sample, not both.")
        if self.distributions is not None:
            missing = [i for i in ids if i not in self.distributions]
            extra = sorted(set(self.distributions) - set(ids))
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"The inputs {missing} have no distribution: give one per "
                    "input, or InputSpace.uniform_on_bounds(parameters)."
                )
            if extra:
                raise ValueError(f"The distributions of {extra} name no input.")
        if self.sample is not None:
            bounds = [(p.min_bound, p.max_bound) for p in self.parameters]
            if self.sample.names != ids or list(self.sample.bounds) != bounds:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"The sample has the inputs {self.sample.names} with the bounds "
                    f"{list(self.sample.bounds)}; the parameters are {ids} with the "
                    f"bounds {bounds}, in this order."
                )
        return self

    @classmethod
    def independent(
        cls,
        parameters: Sequence[CalibrationParameter],
        distributions: Mapping[str, Distribution],
        *,
        initial_condition_remainder: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Independent inputs, each with its distribution.

        Parameters
        ----------
        parameters : Sequence[CalibrationParameter]
            The inputs, in order.
        distributions : Mapping[str, Distribution]
            The distribution of each input, truncated to its bounds.
        initial_condition_remainder : str | None, optional
            The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions
            leave.

        Returns
        -------
        InputSpace
            The input space.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an input has no distribution or is a factor, a distribution
            names no input, or an id repeats.
        """
        return cls(
            parameters=list(parameters),
            distributions=dict(distributions),
            initial_condition_remainder=initial_condition_remainder,
        )

    @classmethod
    def uniform_on_bounds(
        cls,
        parameters: Sequence[CalibrationParameter],
        *,
        initial_condition_remainder: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Independent inputs, each uniform on its bounds; they must be finite.

        Parameters
        ----------
        parameters : Sequence[CalibrationParameter]
            The inputs, in order.
        initial_condition_remainder : str | None, optional
            The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions
            leave.

        Returns
        -------
        InputSpace
            The input space.
        """
        return cls.independent(
            parameters,
            {parameter.id: Uniform() for parameter in parameters},
            initial_condition_remainder=initial_condition_remainder,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_sample(
        cls,
        sample: ParameterSample,
        parameters: Sequence[CalibrationParameter],
        *,
        initial_condition_remainder: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        The draws of a sample, with their weights, such as a posterior.

        Its inputs may depend on each other, so only PRCC and propagation
        take it. The parameters give the type of each value, which a sample
        does not hold.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws.
        parameters : Sequence[CalibrationParameter]
            The inputs, in the order and with the bounds of the sample.
        initial_condition_remainder : str | None, optional
            The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions
            leave.

        Returns
        -------
        InputSpace
            The input space.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the sample's names or bounds are not the parameters'.
        """
        return cls(
            parameters=list(parameters),
            sample=sample,
            initial_condition_remainder=initial_condition_remainder,
        )

    @property
    def names(self) -> list[str]:
        """The ids of the inputs, in order."""
        return [parameter.id for parameter in self.parameters]

    def rust_distributions(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[float]]] | None:
        """The distributions as the Rust runners read them, or None."""
        if self.distributions is None:
            return None
        return [self.distributions[name].rust_prior(name) for name in self.names]
```


The distributions as the Rust runners read them, or None.

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python
def rust_distributions(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[float]]] | None:
    """The distributions as the Rust runners read them, or None."""
    if self.distributions is None:
        return None
    return [self.distributions[name].rust_prior(name) for name in self.names]
```

## Propagation

Bases: `SensitivityMethod[PropagationResult]`

## PropagationResult

Bases: `BaseModel`

The draws of the inputs and what each run gives.

Its `sample` is a `ParameterSample`, so `Predictive(analysis, result.sample, positions)` gives the bands, plots and reports of the propagation, as for a calibration.

Attributes:

| Name      | Type                | Description                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sample`  | `ParameterSample`   | The draws of the inputs: a Latin hypercube of their distributions, or the sample of the input space itself.                  |
| `labels`  | `list[str]`         | The label of each quantity.                                                                                                  |
| `values`  | `list[list[float]]` | The quantities of each run, [run]\[quantity\]: one run per draw, or with a stochastic engine one per replicate of each draw. |
| `weights` | `list[float]`       | The weight of each run; with a stochastic engine each replicate has an equal share of its draw's weight. They sum to 1.      |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python
class PropagationResult(BaseModel):
    """
    The draws of the inputs and what each run gives.

    Its `sample` is a `ParameterSample`, so `Predictive(analysis,
    result.sample, positions)` gives the bands, plots and reports of the
    propagation, as for a calibration.

    Attributes
    ----------
    sample : ParameterSample
        The draws of the inputs: a Latin hypercube of their distributions, or
        the sample of the input space itself.
    labels : list[str]
        The label of each quantity.
    values : list[list[float]]
        The quantities of each run, ``[run][quantity]``: one run per draw, or
        with a stochastic engine one per replicate of each draw.
    weights : list[float]
        The weight of each run; with a stochastic engine each replicate has
        an equal share of its draw's weight. They sum to 1.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    sample: ParameterSample
    labels: list[str]
    values: list[list[float]]
    weights: list[float]

    def summary(self, confidence_level: float) -> list[QuantitySummary]:
        """
        The weighted distribution of each quantity across the runs.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        list[QuantitySummary]
            One summary per quantity, in the order of `labels`.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        if not 0.0 < confidence_level < 1.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The confidence level is strictly between 0 and 1, got "
                f"{confidence_level}"
            )
        levels = [0.5, (1 - confidence_level) / 2, (1 + confidence_level) / 2]
        summaries = []
        for index, label in enumerate(self.labels):
            column = [row[index] for row in self.values]
            median, lower, upper = commol_rs.inference.weighted_quantiles(
                column, self.weights, levels
            )
            summaries.append(
                QuantitySummary(
                    label=label,
                    confidence_level=confidence_level,
                    mean=commol_rs.inference.weighted_mean(column, self.weights),
                    median=median,
                    lower=lower,
                    upper=upper,
                )
            )
        return summaries
```

## PRCC

Bases: `SensitivityMethod[PRCCResult]`

Latin hypercube sampling with partial rank correlation coefficients (Marino et al. 2008): how steadily each quantity rises or falls with each input.

With independent inputs the draws are a Latin hypercube of their distributions; with inputs from a sample, the sample is the design, and the ranks, the correlations and the test read its weights. A `Trajectory` gives the coefficients over the axis.

## PRCCResult

Bases: `BaseModel`

The partial rank correlation of each input with each quantity.

A coefficient near 1 or −1 says the quantity rises or falls steadily with the input once the other inputs are accounted for; near 0, that it does not move steadily with it. The p-value tests the coefficient against 0 with Kish's effective size of the draws.

Attributes:

| Name             | Type                | Description                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sample`         | `ParameterSample`   | The draws the coefficients come from.                                                                         |
| `inputs`         | `list[str]`         | The inputs, in order.                                                                                         |
| `labels`         | `list[str]`         | The label of each quantity.                                                                                   |
| `series`         | `list[str]`         | The series of each quantity: its label, or the name of its Trajectory.                                        |
| `positions`      | \`list\[float       | None\]\`                                                                                                      |
| `coefficients`   | `list[list[float]]` | The PRCC of each input for each quantity, [quantity][input]; NaN for a quantity with one value in every draw. |
| `p_values`       | `list[list[float]]` | The two-sided p-value of each coefficient, [quantity][input].                                                 |
| `effective_size` | `float`             | Kish's effective size of the draws: their number with equal weights.                                          |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`


## Morris

Bases: `SensitivityMethod[MorrisResult]`

Morris screening (Morris 1991), with the `μ*` of Campolongo, Cariboni and Saltelli (2007): which inputs matter, in few runs.

Each trajectory starts at a random level of every input and moves the inputs one at a time, by half the levels; the levels are the centres of strata of equal probability of each distribution. It needs independent inputs: a step that moves one input breaks the dependence of a sample.

Attributes:

| Name           | Type             | Description                                                                 |
| -------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trajectories` | `int`            | The number of trajectories; each runs one more point than there are inputs. |
| `levels`       | `int`            | The number of levels of each input; even, at least 2.                       |
| `quantities`   | `list[Quantity]` | What each run is reduced to.                                                |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python

    """
    Morris screening (Morris 1991), with the ``μ*`` of Campolongo, Cariboni
    and Saltelli (2007): which inputs matter, in few runs.

    Each trajectory starts at a random level of every input and moves the
    inputs one at a time, by half the levels; the levels are the centres of
    strata of equal probability of each distribution. It needs independent
    inputs: a step that moves one input breaks the dependence of a sample.

    Attributes
    ----------
    trajectories : int
        The number of trajectories; each runs one more point than there are
        inputs.
    levels : int
        The number of levels of each input; even, at least 2.
    quantities : list[Quantity]
        What each run is reduced to.
    """

    trajectories: int = Field(ge=1, description="The number of trajectories.")
    levels: int = Field(ge=2, description="The number of levels; even.")
    quantities: list[Quantity] = Field(
        min_length=1, description="What each run is reduced to."
    )
```

## MorrisResult

Bases: `BaseModel`

The Morris indices of each input for each quantity.

The elementary effects are on the scale of probabilities: a step moves an input by half the range of `F(x)`, so the indices of inputs of different units compare. Rank the inputs by `mu_star`; a `sigma` near or above `mu_star` says the effect of the input depends on the other inputs or is not linear.

Attributes:

| `mu_star` | `list[list[float]]` | The mean absolute elementary effect, [quantity][input].                                       |
| `sigma`   | `list[list[float]]` | The standard deviation of the elementary effects, [quantity][input]; NaN with one trajectory. |
| `runs`    | `int`               | The number of points run: one more than the inputs per trajectory.                            |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

## Sobol

Bases: `SensitivityMethod[SobolResult]`

Sobol indices on the design of Saltelli (2010): first-order indices by the estimator of Saltelli (2010) and total indices by the estimator of Jansen (1999), with intervals from a bootstrap of the rows.

The base matrices hold independent Monte Carlo draws, so the bootstrap intervals are valid. It needs independent inputs: with dependent inputs the indices lose their meaning and no longer add up; PRCC and propagation take a sample.

Attributes:

| Name               | Type             | Description                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `base_draws`       | `int`            | The rows of each base matrix; the analysis runs base_draws · (inputs + 2) points. |
| `bootstrap`        | `int`            | The bootstrap replicates of the intervals, at least 2.                            |
| `confidence_level` | `float`          | The level of the intervals, strictly between 0 and 1.                             |
| `quantities`       | `list[Quantity]` | What each run is reduced to.                                                      |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python

    Jansen (1999), with intervals from a bootstrap of the rows.
```

## SobolResult

Bases: `BaseModel`

The Sobol indices of each input for each quantity, with their bootstrap intervals.

The first-order index is the share of the variance of the quantity the input explains alone; the total index adds every interaction the input takes part in. A total index near 0 says the input can be fixed; a total index well above the first-order one says the input acts through interactions.

Attributes:

| Name                       | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inputs`                   | `list[str]`         | The inputs, in order.                                                                                                                        |
| `labels`                   | `list[str]`         | The label of each quantity.                                                                                                                  |
| `confidence_level`         | `float`             | The level of the intervals.                                                                                                                  |
| `first, total`             | `list[list[float]]` | The first-order and total indices, [quantity][input]; NaN for a quantity of no variance.                                                     |
| `first_lower, first_upper` | `list[list[float]]` | The ends of the interval of each first-order index; NaN when a bootstrap replicate of the rows has no variance, which more base_draws avoid. |
| `total_lower, total_upper` | `list[list[float]]` | The ends of the interval of each total index.                                                                                                |
| `runs`                     | `int`               | The number of points run: base_draws · (inputs + 2).                                                                                         |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python

    input explains alone; the total index adds every interaction the input
    takes part in. A total index near 0 says the input can be fixed; a total
    index well above the first-order one says the input acts through
    interactions.

    Attributes
    ----------
    inputs : list[str]
        The inputs, in order.
    labels : list[str]
        The label of each quantity.
    confidence_level : float
        The level of the intervals.

        The ends of the interval of each first-order index; NaN when a

    total_lower, total_upper : list[list[float]]
```

## PolynomialChaos

Bases: `SensitivityMethod[ChaosResult]`

A polynomial chaos expansion (Sudret 2008): a polynomial surrogate of each quantity, and the Sobol indices of its coefficients, in far fewer runs than `Sobol` when the quantity is smooth.

Every input goes to `u = F(x)`, uniform on `[0, 1]` through its distribution, so one basis of orthonormal Legendre polynomials fits every distribution, truncated ones included. The coefficients come from least squares on a Latin hypercube; the leave-one-out error says how well the expansion predicts the model. It needs independent inputs.

Attributes:

| Name         | Type             | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `degree`     | `int`            | The total degree of the basis: in k inputs it has (k + degree)! / (k! degree!) terms.                       |
| `draws`      | `int`            | The points of the Latin hypercube; more than the terms, and two or three times as many is the usual choice. |
| `quantities` | `list[Quantity]` | What each run is reduced to.                                                                                |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python
class PolynomialChaos(SensitivityMethod[ChaosResult]):
    """
    A polynomial chaos expansion (Sudret 2008): a polynomial surrogate of
    each quantity, and the Sobol indices of its coefficients, in far fewer
    runs than `Sobol` when the quantity is smooth.

    Every input goes to ``u = F(x)``, uniform on ``[0, 1]`` through its
    distribution, so one basis of orthonormal Legendre polynomials fits every
    distribution, truncated ones included. The coefficients come from least
    squares on a Latin hypercube; the leave-one-out error says how well the
    expansion predicts the model. It needs independent inputs.

    Attributes
    ----------
    degree : int
        The total degree of the basis: in ``k`` inputs it has
        ``(k + degree)! / (k! degree!)`` terms.
    draws : int
        The points of the Latin hypercube; more than the terms, and two or
        three times as many is the usual choice.
    quantities : list[Quantity]
        What each run is reduced to.
    """

    degree: int = Field(ge=1, description="The total degree of the basis.")
    draws: int = Field(ge=2, description="Points of the Latin hypercube.")
    quantities: list[Quantity] = Field(
        min_length=1, description="What each run is reduced to."
    )
```

## ChaosResult

Bases: `BaseModel`

A polynomial chaos expansion of each quantity, its accuracy and the Sobol indices of its coefficients.

The expansion is a surrogate of the model: `predict` gives the quantities at any values of the inputs inside their bounds, at the cost of a polynomial. Read `loo_error` first: the indices are those of the expansion, and they are those of the model only as far as the expansion predicts it.

Attributes:

| Name             | Type                | Description                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inputs`         | `list[str]`         | The inputs, in order.                                                                                              |
| `input_space`    | `InputSpace`        | The inputs and their distributions, which predict maps values through.                                             |
| `labels`         | `list[str]`         | The label of each quantity.                                                                                        |
| `degree`         | `int`               | The total degree of the basis.                                                                                     |
| `indices`        | `list[list[int]]`   | The degree of each input in each term, [term][input]; term 0 is the constant.                                      |
| `coefficients`   | `list[list[float]]` | The coefficient of each term for each quantity, [quantity][term], on orthonormal Legendre polynomials of u = F(x). |
| `loo_error`      | `list[float]`       | The leave-one-out error of each quantity, relative to its variance; NaN for a quantity of no variance.             |
| `mean, variance` | `list[float]`       | The mean and the variance of each quantity under the expansion.                                                    |
| `first, total`   | `list[list[float]]` | The first-order and total Sobol indices, [quantity][input]; NaN for a quantity of no variance.                     |
| `runs`           | `int`               | The number of points run.                                                                                          |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python
class ChaosResult(BaseModel):
    """
    A polynomial chaos expansion of each quantity, its accuracy and the
    Sobol indices of its coefficients.

    The expansion is a surrogate of the model: `predict` gives the
    quantities at any values of the inputs inside their bounds, at the cost
    of a polynomial. Read
    `loo_error` first: the indices are those of the expansion, and they are
    those of the model only as far as the expansion predicts it.

    Attributes
    ----------
    inputs : list[str]
        The inputs, in order.
    input_space : InputSpace
        The inputs and their distributions, which `predict` maps values
        through.
    labels : list[str]
        The label of each quantity.
    degree : int
        The total degree of the basis.
    indices : list[list[int]]
        The degree of each input in each term, ``[term][input]``; term 0 is
        the constant.
    coefficients : list[list[float]]
        The coefficient of each term for each quantity, ``[quantity][term]``,
        on orthonormal Legendre polynomials of ``u = F(x)``.
    loo_error : list[float]
        The leave-one-out error of each quantity, relative to its variance;
        NaN for a quantity of no variance.
    mean, variance : list[float]
        The mean and the variance of each quantity under the expansion.
    first, total : list[list[float]]
        The first-order and total Sobol indices, ``[quantity][input]``; NaN
        for a quantity of no variance.
    runs : int
        The number of points run.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    inputs: list[str]
    input_space: InputSpace
    labels: list[str]
    degree: int
    indices: list[list[int]]
    coefficients: list[list[float]]
    loo_error: list[float]
    mean: list[float]
    variance: list[float]
    first: list[list[float]]
    total: list[list[float]]
    runs: int

    def predict(self, values: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        The quantities the expansion gives at each set of input values.

        Parameters
        ----------
        values : Sequence[Sequence[float]]
            One value per input, in the order of `inputs`, for each point,
            each inside the bounds of its input.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            The value of each quantity at each point, ``[point][quantity]``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a point has not one value per input or a value outside the
            bounds of its input, or the coefficients do not fit the degree.
        """
        return commol_rs.inference.chaos_evaluate(
            engine_state.rust_parameters(self.input_space.parameters),
            self.input_space.rust_distributions() or [],
            self.degree,
            self.coefficients,
            [list(point) for point in values],
        )
```

## Gain

Bases: `_OneScalar`

The value at `end` minus the value at `start`: what entered a cumulative output over `(start, end]`, as an observation with the window `end - start` reads it.

Attributes:

| Name    | Type    | Description                         |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `start` | `float` | The start of the window.            |
| `end`   | `float` | The end of the window, after start. |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/global_sensitivity.py`

```python
class Gain(_OneScalar):
    """
    The value at `end` minus the value at `start`: what entered a cumulative
    output over ``(start, end]``, as an observation with the window
    ``end - start`` reads it.

    Attributes
    ----------
    start : float
        The start of the window.
    end : float
        The end of the window, after `start`.
    """

    rust_kind: ClassVar[str] = "gain"
    kind: Literal["gain"] = "gain"
    start: Position = Field(description="The start of the window.")
    end: Position = Field(description="The end of the window.")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def end_after_start(self) -> Self:
        """A window ends after it starts."""
        if self.end <= self.start:
            raise ValueError(
                f"A gain ends after it starts, got start {self.start} and end "
                f"{self.end}"
            )
        return self

    def default_label(self) -> str:
        """The gain of `outputs` over the window."""
        return f"{self.output_name} gain over ({self.start:g}, {self.end:g}]"

    def rust_quantity(self) -> RustQuantity:
        """The kind, the outputs, the start and the end."""
        return (self.rust_kind, self.output_list, [self.start, self.end])
```

```python
class Trajectory(_AtPositions):

    The value at each position: one `ValueAt` per position, for an analysis
    over the axis.

    Attributes
    ----------

    kind: Literal["trajectory"] = "trajectory"

        ]
```

# Simulation API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

Runs a model and reads its outputs. Guide: [Running Simulations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/index.md).

## Simulation

A Facade for running a simulation from a defined Model.

The engine follows the model: `run` and `engine` rebuild it when `model_definition` no longer serializes to the JSON the engine was built from, for example after `Model.update_parameters`.

Source code in `commol/api/simulation.py`

```python
class Simulation:
    """
    A Facade for running a simulation from a defined Model.

    The engine follows the model: ``run`` and ``engine`` rebuild it when
    ``model_definition`` no longer serializes to the JSON the engine was built
    from, for example after ``Model.update_parameters``.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: Model):
        """
        Initializes the simulation engine from a Pydantic Model definition.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            A fully constructed and validated model object, of any kind.
            None values for parameters/initial conditions if used for calibration.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If the structure of the model is not a `ModelStructure`.

        """
        if not isinstance(model.structure, ModelStructure):
            raise TypeError(
                f"The structure of model '{model.name}' is a "
                f"{type(model.structure).__name__}, not a ModelStructure. A model "
                "holds the structure of its kind, such as an Aggregate."
            )
        logger.info(f"Initializing Simulation with model: '{model.name}'")
        self.model_definition: Model = model
        self._build_engine(model.model_dump_json())

    def _build_engine(self, model_json: str) -> None:
        """Build the engine and its output names from a model JSON."""
        self._model_json: str = model_json
        self._engine: "EngineProtocol" = build_engine(model_json)
        self._simulation_outputs: list[str] = self._engine.output_names
        logger.info(
            f"Simulation engine ready. Outputs: {len(self._simulation_outputs)}"
        )

    def _sync_engine(self) -> None:
        """Rebuild the engine when the model changed since it was built."""
        model_json = self.model_definition.model_dump_json()
        if model_json != self._model_json:
            logger.info("Model changed since the engine was built; rebuilding it.")
            self._build_engine(model_json)

    def _validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self, model: Model) -> None:
        """
        Validates that every parameter, and every value of the model kind, has
        a value (is calibrated).

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model to validate.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any parameter, or any value of the model kind such as an
            initial condition, has a None value.
        """
        uncalibrated_params = model.get_uncalibrated_parameters()
        uncalibrated_ics = model.structure.uncalibrated_values()

        errors = []
        if uncalibrated_params:
            errors.append(
                f"Parameters requiring calibration: {', '.join(uncalibrated_params)}"
            )
        if uncalibrated_ics:
            errors.append(
                f"Initial conditions requiring calibration: "
                f"{', '.join(uncalibrated_ics)}"
            )

        if errors:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot run Simulation: {'; '.join(errors)}. "
                f"Please calibrate these values before running a simulation."
            )

    @property
    def is_stochastic(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the engine of the model draws random numbers."""
        return commol_rs.engine.EngineType(
            self.model_definition.engine.type
        ).is_stochastic

    def _seed_run(self, seed: int | None) -> int | None:
        """Seed the engine of a stochastic model; None for a deterministic one."""
        if not self.is_stochastic:
            return None
        seed = draw_seed() if seed is None else check_seed(seed)
        self._engine.set_seed(seed)
        return seed

    def run(self, num_steps: int, *, seed: int | None = None) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state on its default grid.

        Every call starts at position 0 with the current ``model_definition``,
        so two calls with the same model, and the same seed for a stochastic
        engine, give the same result. To continue a run, call
        ``simulation.engine.step()``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        num_steps : int
            The number of steps: the results hold the positions
            ``0, 1, ..., num_steps``.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of a stochastic engine, a whole number from 0 to
            ``2**64 - 1``. None draws one, which ``results.seed`` keeps, so
            every run can be repeated. A deterministic engine ignores it.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, the positions, and the
            seed of a stochastic run.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a step leaves an amount below zero; the message names the
            compartment, the step and the flows out of it.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value, or the seed is
            not a whole number from 0 to ``2**64 - 1``.
        RuntimeError
            If a rate cannot be evaluated or is not a number; the message
            names the flow and the position.
        """
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        used_seed = self._seed_run(seed)
        self._engine.reset()
        logger.info(f"Running simulation for {num_steps} steps.")
        start = time.time()
        positions, rows = self._engine.run(num_steps)
        logger.info(f"Simulation complete. It took {time.time() - start} seconds.")
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(
            positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows, seed=used_seed
        )

    def run_at(
        self, at: Sequence[float], *, seed: int | None = None
    ) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state and reports at given positions.

        The positions are on the axis, the independent variable of the model.
        The engine decides which positions its model type reports at: a
        DifferentialEquations model at any finite, non-negative position, from
        the dense output of its solver; a DifferenceEquations model only at
        integer steps.

        Parameters
        ----------
        at : Sequence[float]
            Sorted, unique positions to report at.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of a stochastic engine; see `run`.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, the positions, and the
            seed of a stochastic run.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a step leaves an amount below zero; the message names the
            compartment, the step and the flows out of it.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value, the positions are
            not sorted and unique, or the engine does not report at one of them;
            the message is the engine's.
        RuntimeError
            If a rate cannot be evaluated or is not a number; the message
            names the flow and the position.
        """
        positions = [float(position) for position in at]
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        used_seed = self._seed_run(seed)
        self._engine.reset()
        rows = self._engine.run_at(positions)
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(
            positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows, seed=used_seed
        )

    def replicates(self, n: int, *, seed: int | None = None) -> "ReplicateRuns":
        """
        Replicates of the runs of a stochastic engine.

        The returned object has ``run`` and ``run_at``, as `Simulation`, and
        they return `SimulationReplicates`: ``n`` runs, each with its own seed,
        run in parallel in the engine. Replicate ``i`` takes the seed derived
        from ``seed`` and ``i`` (the SplitMix64 of ``seed + i``), so it gives
        the same run however many replicates run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        n : int
            How many replicates, at least 1.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from, a whole number from 0 to
            ``2**64 - 1``. None draws one, which the replicates keep.

        Returns
        -------
        ReplicateRuns
            The runner of the replicates.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the engine is deterministic (every replicate would be equal),
            ``n`` is below 1, or the seed is not valid.
        """
        if not self.is_stochastic:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {self.model_definition.engine.type} engine is deterministic: "
                "every replicate would be equal. Replicates need a stochastic engine."
            )
        if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"The number of replicates is at least 1, got {n!r}.")
        return ReplicateRuns(self, n, draw_seed() if seed is None else check_seed(seed))

    @property
    def engine(self) -> "EngineProtocol":
        """
        The engine for the current ``model_definition``.

        It is rebuilt, at step 0, when the model changed since it was built.
        Otherwise it is the same object, in the state the last ``run`` or
        ``step`` left it.
        """
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._engine

    @property
    def simulation_outputs(self) -> list[str]:
        """Names of the columns returned by simulation runs."""
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._simulation_outputs

    def outputs_for(self, id: str) -> list[str]:
        """
        Names of the outputs a source id expands into.

        The structure of the model groups its outputs by source
        (`ModelStructure.outputs_by_source`): for an aggregate model, by
        bin and accumulator.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            A source id, such as a bin id or an accumulator id.

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            Output names for that id, in the order the engine reports them.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If `id` is not a source of the model.
        """
        model = self.model_definition
        outputs = model.structure.outputs_by_source(model)
        if id not in outputs:
            raise KeyError(
                f"'{id}' is not a bin or accumulator of model "
                f"'{self.model_definition.name}'. Available: {sorted(outputs)}"
            )
        return outputs[id]

    def group_outputs(self, ids: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """
        Group output names by the bin or accumulator they belong to.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[str]]
            Each id mapped to its output names, keeping the order given.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model.
        """
        return {id: self.outputs_for(id) for id in ids}

    def total_series(
        self,
        results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
        ids: Iterable[str],
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]
            Simulation results, such as those of `run` or `run_at`.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One value per position of `results`.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        """
        names = [name for id in ids for name in self.outputs_for(id)]
        missing = [name for name in names if name not in results]
        if missing:
            raise KeyError(f"Missing output series in results: {sorted(missing)}")
        if not names:
            return []
        return [
            sum(values)
            for values in zip(*(results[name] for name in names), strict=True)
        ]

    def windowed_totals(
        self,
        results: SimulationResults,
        ids: Iterable[str],
        window: float,
        at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Amount the given accumulators gained over each window.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : SimulationResults
            Simulation results, with their positions.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Accumulator ids whose outputs are summed before windowing.
        window : float
            Length of one window on the axis.
        at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
            Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete
            window of the results (:func:`commol.window_ends`). Pass the
            observation positions to reproduce exactly the values a
            calibration used.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One increment per window.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        ValueError
            If `window` is not positive, or the results have no value at the
            end or the start of a requested window.
        """
        return windowed_totals(
            self.total_series(results, ids), results.positions, window, at
        )
```
