## ConformalMethod

Bases: `UncertaintyMethod[ConformalResult]`

What every conformal method takes: a score, the pooling of its quantiles, and a level, none of them with a default.

Attributes:

| Name    | Type                             | Description                                                                                                                                    |
| ------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `score` | `{absolute, normalized, spread}` | The nonconformity score. "normalized" needs by="all": per series its factor is one constant, so its intervals would equal those of "absolute". |
| `by`    | `{series, all}`                  | Whether each series gets its own quantile, or all series share one.                                                                            |
| `level` | `float`                          | The level of the intervals, strictly between 0 and 1.                                                                                          |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/conformal.py`

```python
class ConformalMethod(UncertaintyMethod[ConformalResult]):
    """
    What every conformal method takes: a score, the pooling of its
    quantiles, and a level, none of them with a default.

    Attributes
    ----------
    score : {"absolute", "normalized", "spread"}
        The nonconformity score. ``"normalized"`` needs ``by="all"``: per
        series its factor is one constant, so its intervals would equal those
        of ``"absolute"``.
    by : {"series", "all"}
        Whether each series gets its own quantile, or all series share one.
    level : float
        The level of the intervals, strictly between 0 and 1.
    """

    score: ConformalScore = Field(description="The nonconformity score.")
    by: Pooling = Field(description="Which scores each quantile reads.")
    level: float = Field(gt=0.0, lt=1.0, description="The level of the intervals.")

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def check_score_and_by(cls, data: object) -> object:
        """Check, in Rust, that `score` and `by` are given and fit together."""
        if isinstance(data, Mapping):

            def name(key: str) -> str | None:
                value = data.get(key)
                return None if value is None else str(value)

            commol_rs.inference.check_conformal_settings(name("score"), name("by"))
        return data
```

## SplitConformal

Bases: `ConformalMethod`

Split conformal prediction.

It fits the problem's observations and scores `calibration_data`, observations held out of the fit. When the scores of the held-out and of new observations are exchangeable, each interval covers a new observation with probability at least `level`.

Attributes:

| Name               | Type                      | Description                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `calibration_data` | `list[ObservedDataPoint]` | Held-out observations; each of their series gets intervals.   |
| `positions`        | `list[float]`             | Where the intervals are, for each series of calibration_data. |
| `sample`           | \`ParameterSample         | None\`                                                        |
| `starts`           | `int`                     | Starts of the fit (default 1).                                |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/conformal.py`

```python
class SplitConformal(ConformalMethod):
    """
    Split conformal prediction.

    It fits the problem's observations and scores `calibration_data`,
    observations held out of the fit. When the scores of the held-out and of
    new observations are exchangeable, each interval covers a new
    observation with probability at least `level`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    calibration_data : list[ObservedDataPoint]
        Held-out observations; each of their series gets intervals.
    positions : list[float]
        Where the intervals are, for each series of `calibration_data`.
    sample : ParameterSample | None
        None: the prediction is the fit. A sample: the prediction is the
        weighted median of its predictive, and its weighted standard
        deviation is the spread of ``score="spread"``.
    starts : int
        Starts of the fit (default 1).
    """

    calibration_data: list[ObservedDataPoint] = Field(
        min_length=1, description="Held-out observations."
    )
    positions: list[float] = Field(min_length=1, description="Where the intervals are.")
    sample: ParameterSample | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The sample whose predictive predicts."
    )
    starts: int = Field(default=1, ge=1, description="Starts of the fit.")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_spread(self) -> Self:
        """Reject ``score="spread"`` without a sample."""
        _no_spread_without_sample(self)
        return self
```

## RollingConformal

Bases: `ConformalMethod`

Rolling-origin conformal prediction: intervals ahead of the data, one quantile per horizon.

Each origin fits the observations at or before it and scores the later ones. Horizon `k` is the `k`-th observation of a series after the origin: a count, not a distance on the axis.

Attributes:

| Name        | Type          | Description                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `origins`   | `list[float]` | The positions of the origins.                                                |
| `positions` | `list[float]` | Where the intervals are, all after the data; the k-th position is horizon k. |
| `starts`    | `int`         | Starts of each fit (default 1).                                              |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/conformal.py`

```python
class RollingConformal(ConformalMethod):
    """
    Rolling-origin conformal prediction: intervals ahead of the data, one
    quantile per horizon.

    Each origin fits the observations at or before it and scores the later
    ones. Horizon ``k`` is the ``k``-th observation of a series after the
    origin: a count, not a distance on the axis.

    Attributes
    ----------
    origins : list[float]
        The positions of the origins.
    positions : list[float]
        Where the intervals are, all after the data; the ``k``-th position
        is horizon ``k``.
    starts : int
        Starts of each fit (default 1).
    """

    origins: list[float] = Field(min_length=1, description="The origins.")
    positions: list[float] = Field(min_length=1, description="Where the intervals are.")
    starts: int = Field(default=1, ge=1, description="Starts of each fit.")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_spread(self) -> Self:
        """Reject ``score="spread"``: one fit per origin has no spread."""
        if self.score == "spread":
            raise ValueError(
                "RollingConformal fits once per origin, so its predictions have no "
                'spread for score="spread"; use "absolute" or "normalized"'
            )
        return self
```

## JackknifePlus

Bases: `ConformalMethod`

Jackknife+ (Barber et al. 2021) with blocks: one refit per block left out, and intervals from the left-out residuals and predictions.

With exchangeable blocks it covers at least `1 − 2α` when each block holds one observation, and the CV+ bound with `K` blocks otherwise.

## EnbPI

Bases: `ConformalMethod`

Ensemble batch prediction intervals (Xu and Xie 2021).

Each replicate draws blocks with replacement and fits. The replicates that left out the block of an observation give its leave-one-out prediction and score; their mean over every observation is the point prediction.

## AdaptiveConformal

Bases: `ConformalMethod`

Adaptive conformal inference (Gibbs and Candès 2021).

It fits the problem's observations and walks `stream` in order of position. The interval of each point is the quantile, at the working level `1 − α_t`, of the scores of the earlier points of the stream; then the working level moves by `α_{t+1} = α_t + γ (α − err_t)`. The long-run share of misses tends to `α`, with no assumption on the data.

Attributes:

| Name     | Type                      | Description                                  |
| -------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `step`   | `float`                   | The step γ of the working level, positive.   |
| `stream` | `list[ObservedDataPoint]` | The observations that arrive after the data. |
| `sample` | \`ParameterSample         | None\`                                       |
| `starts` | `int`                     | Starts of the fit (default 1).               |

Source code in `commol/context/inference/conformal.py`

```python
class AdaptiveConformal(ConformalMethod):
    """
    Adaptive conformal inference (Gibbs and Candès 2021).

    It fits the problem's observations and walks `stream` in order of
    position. The interval of each point is the quantile, at the working
    level ``1 − α_t``, of the scores of the earlier points of the stream;
    then the working level moves by ``α_{t+1} = α_t + γ (α − err_t)``. The
    long-run share of misses tends to ``α``, with no assumption on the data.

    Attributes
    ----------
    step : float
        The step ``γ`` of the working level, positive.
    stream : list[ObservedDataPoint]
        The observations that arrive after the data.
    sample : ParameterSample | None
        As in `SplitConformal`.
    starts : int
        Starts of the fit (default 1).
    """

    step: float = Field(gt=0.0, description="The step of the working level.")
    stream: list[ObservedDataPoint] = Field(
        min_length=1, description="The observations that arrive."
    )

        default=None, description="The sample whose predictive predicts."
    )
    starts: int = Field(default=1, ge=1, description="Starts of the fit.")

    def check_spread(self) -> Self:

        return self
```

## Scores and intervals

## scores

Scores of a predictive against observations.

Every score is computed in Rust, per observation and per series: from each draw's value of the observations (`Predictive.at_observations`), or, for the log score, from the density of the observation models at each draw's prediction. Which observations to score, for example the ones held out of the calibration, and the observation noise are arguments with no default: a band of the model (`NoNoise`) compared with data covers less than its level.

### Classes

One score of a predictive at a set of observations.

Attributes:

| Name              | Type               | Description                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `per_series`      | `dict[str, float]` | The mean score of each series (observation label), in order of first appearance. |
| `mean`            | `float`            | The mean over every observation.                                                 |

Source code in `commol/api/inference/scores.py`

```python
def coverage(
    predictive: Predictive,
    observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint],
    noise: ObservationNoise,
    confidence_level: float,
) -> Score:
    """
    The empirical coverage of the central interval of `confidence_level`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    predictive : Predictive
        The predictive.
    observations : Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
        The observations to score.
    noise : NoNoise | ResidualNoise | DistributionNoise
        The observation noise of the draws (`Predictive.at_observations`).
    confidence_level : float
        Strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    Score
        1 for each observation inside its interval, 0 outside; the means are
        the coverage. A calibrated interval covers about `confidence_level`.
    """
    draws = predictive.at_observations(observations, noise)
    return _score(draws, draws.rust_draws.coverage(draws.observed, confidence_level))
```

```python
    predictive: Predictive,
    observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint],
    noise: ObservationNoise,
    confidence_level: float,
```

#### weighted_interval_score

```python
weighted_interval_score(predictive: Predictive, observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint], noise: ObservationNoise, confidence_levels: Sequence[float]) -> Score
```

The weighted interval score of Bracher et al. (2021).

`(½|y − m| + Σₖ (αₖ/2) IS_αₖ) / (K + ½)`, with `m` the median and `αₖ = 1 − cₖ` for each confidence level `cₖ`.

Parameters:

| Name                | Type                          | Description                          | Default             |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------- |
| `predictive`        | `Predictive`                  | The predictive.                      | *required*          |
| `observations`      | `Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]` | The observations to score.           | *required*          |
| `noise`             | \`NoNoise                     | ResidualNoise                        | DistributionNoise\` |
| `confidence_levels` | `Sequence[float]`             | The levels of the central intervals. | *required*          |

Returns:

| Type    | Description      |
| ------- | ---------------- |
| `Score` | Lower is better. |

References

Bracher, J., Ray, E. L., Gneiting, T., & Reich, N. G. (2021). Evaluating epidemic forecasts in an interval format. PLOS Computational Biology, 17(2), e1008618. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008618

Source code in `commol/api/inference/scores.py`

```python
def weighted_interval_score(
    predictive: Predictive,
    observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint],
    noise: ObservationNoise,
    confidence_levels: Sequence[float],
) -> Score:
    """
    The weighted interval score of Bracher et al. (2021).

    ``(½|y − m| + Σₖ (αₖ/2) IS_αₖ) / (K + ½)``, with ``m`` the median and
    ``αₖ = 1 − cₖ`` for each confidence level ``cₖ``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    predictive : Predictive
        The predictive.
    observations : Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
        The observations to score.
    noise : NoNoise | ResidualNoise | DistributionNoise
        The observation noise of the draws (`Predictive.at_observations`).
    confidence_levels : Sequence[float]
        The levels of the central intervals.

    Returns
    -------
    Score
        Lower is better.

    References
    ----------
    Bracher, J., Ray, E. L., Gneiting, T., & Reich, N. G. (2021). Evaluating
    epidemic forecasts in an interval format. PLOS Computational Biology,
    17(2), e1008618. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008618
    """
    draws = predictive.at_observations(observations, noise)
    return _score(
        draws,
        draws.rust_draws.weighted_interval_score(
            draws.observed, [float(c) for c in confidence_levels]
        ),
    )
```

#### log_score

```python
log_score(predictive: Predictive, observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint], noise: DistributionNoise) -> Score
```

The log score of each observation: the log density of its value under the predictive.

The predictive density is the mixture over the draws of the observation models, `log Σ_d w_d · p(y | μ_d)`, with `μ_d` the prediction of draw `d` and its noise parameters. It needs the densities of the models, so only `DistributionNoise` has one. A proper scoring rule; higher is better, and an observation the predictive gives no mass scores `-inf`.

Parameters:

| Name           | Type                          | Description                                           | Default    |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `predictive`   | `Predictive`                  | The predictive, of a problem with observation_models. | *required* |
| `observations` | `Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]` | The observations to score.                            | *required* |
| `noise`        | `DistributionNoise`           | The observation models of the problem.                | *required* |

Returns:

| Type    | Description                        |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `Score` | The log score of each observation. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TypeError`  | If noise is not DistributionNoise.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ValueError` | If the problem has a loss, an observation names an unknown output or factor or a series with no observation model, or the predictive is of a sensitivity analysis, which has no observation models. |

Source code in `commol/api/inference/scores.py`

```python
def log_score(
    predictive: Predictive,
    observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint],
    noise: DistributionNoise,
) -> Score:
    """
    The log score of each observation: the log density of its value under
    the predictive.

    The predictive density is the mixture over the draws of the observation
    models, ``log Σ_d w_d · p(y | μ_d)``, with ``μ_d`` the prediction of draw
    ``d`` and its noise parameters. It needs the densities of the models, so
    only `DistributionNoise` has one. A proper scoring rule; higher is
    better, and an observation the predictive gives no mass scores ``-inf``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    predictive : Predictive
        The predictive, of a problem with ``observation_models``.
    observations : Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
        The observations to score.
    noise : DistributionNoise
        The observation models of the problem.

    Returns
    -------
    Score
        The log score of each observation.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If `noise` is not `DistributionNoise`.
    ValueError
        If the problem has a loss, an observation names an unknown output or
        factor or a series with no observation model, or the predictive is of
        a sensitivity analysis, which has no observation models.
    """
    if not isinstance(noise, DistributionNoise):
        raise TypeError(
            f"The log score needs the density of the observation models, so it "
            f"takes DistributionNoise(); {type(noise).__name__} has no density."
        )
    values = predictive.source.rust_log_score(predictive.sample, list(observations))
    return _score_of(observations, values)
```

## weighted_quantiles

```python
weighted_quantiles(values: Sequence[float], levels: Sequence[float], weights: Sequence[float] | None = None) -> list[float]
```

Quantiles of weighted values, by the one convention of commol.

The quantile is the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution, interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights. With equal weights it equals `numpy.percentile(..., method="hazen")`. A weight of zero removes a value.

Parameters:

| Name      | Type              | Description                            | Default                                                                    |
| --------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `values`  | `Sequence[float]` | The values.                            | *required*                                                                 |
| `levels`  | `Sequence[float]` | Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1. | *required*                                                                 |
| `weights` | \`Sequence[float] | None\`                                 | One non-negative weight per value, of any scale. None gives equal weights. |

Returns:

| Type          | Description             |
| ------------- | ----------------------- |
| `list[float]` | One quantile per level. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If the lengths differ, no weight is positive or a level is not in [0, 1]. |

Source code in `commol/api/inference/intervals.py`

```python
def weighted_quantiles(
    values: Sequence[float],
    levels: Sequence[float],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Quantiles of weighted values, by the one convention of commol.

    The quantile is the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution,
    interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights. With equal
    weights it equals ``numpy.percentile(..., method="hazen")``. A weight of
    zero removes a value.

    Parameters
    ----------
    values : Sequence[float]
        The values.
    levels : Sequence[float]
        Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1.
    weights : Sequence[float] | None, optional
        One non-negative weight per value, of any scale. None gives equal
        weights.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One quantile per level.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the lengths differ, no weight is positive or a level is not in
        ``[0, 1]``.
    """
    values = [float(value) for value in values]
    if weights is None:
        weights = [1.0] * len(values)
    return commol_rs.inference.weighted_quantiles(
        values, [float(w) for w in weights], [float(level) for level in levels]
    )
```

## member_statistics

Spread of one quantity across the members of an ensemble.

Each member must already be reduced to the quantity of interest, so that the reported interval is a quantile of member values (:func:`weighted_quantiles`).

Parameters:

| Name               | Type              | Description                                                          | Default                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `per_member`       | \`Sequence[float] | Sequence\[Sequence[float]\]                                          | NDArray\`                                                                                            |
| `confidence_level` | `float`           | Confidence level of the reported interval, strictly between 0 and 1. | *required*                                                                                           |
| `weights`          | \`Sequence[float] | None\`                                                               | One weight per member, such as the weights of a :class:~commol.Predictive. None gives equal weights. |

Returns:

| Type               | Description                |
| ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| \`dict[str, float] | dict\[str, list[float]\]\` |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                                                        |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If confidence_level is out of range, per_member is empty, or the weights do not match the members. |

Source code in `commol/api/inference/intervals.py`

```python
def member_statistics(
    per_member: EnsembleValues,
    confidence_level: float,
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, float] | dict[str, list[float]] | dict[str, float | list[float]]:
    """
    Spread of one quantity across the members of an ensemble.

    Each member must already be reduced to the quantity of interest, so that
    the reported interval is a quantile of member values
    (:func:`weighted_quantiles`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    per_member : Sequence[float] | Sequence[Sequence[float]] | NDArray
        One entry per ensemble member. Entries may be scalars, in which case
        every returned statistic is a scalar, or equal-length series, in which
        case every returned statistic is a series reduced across members at
        each position. A numpy array is accepted, but its rank is not visible
        to a type checker; pass a list of lists for a precise return type.
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the reported interval, strictly between 0 and 1.
    weights : Sequence[float] | None, optional
        One weight per member, such as the weights of a
        :class:`~commol.Predictive`. None gives equal weights.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, float] | dict[str, list[float]]
        Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
        ``max``. Scalar members give scalar statistics, series members give
        series statistics. ``min`` and ``max`` are over the members of
        positive weight.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is out of range, ``per_member`` is empty, or
        the weights do not match the members.
    """
    lower_point, upper_point = ci_percentiles(confidence_level)
    values = np.asarray(per_member, dtype=float)
    if values.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("per_member must hold at least one ensemble member.")
    member_weights = (
        [1.0] * values.shape[0] if weights is None else [float(w) for w in weights]
    )
    if len(member_weights) != values.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"One weight per member: {values.shape[0]} members, "
            f"{len(member_weights)} weights."
        )
    levels = [0.0, lower_point / 100.0, 0.5, upper_point / 100.0, 1.0]
    columns = values.reshape(values.shape[0], -1).T
    table = [
        weighted_quantiles(column.tolist(), levels, member_weights)
        for column in columns
    ]
    means = [
        commol_rs.inference.weighted_mean(column.tolist(), member_weights)
        for column in columns
    ]

    def shaped(per_column: list[float]) -> float | list[float]:
        return per_column[0] if values.ndim == 1 else per_column

    return {
        "mean": shaped(means),
        "median": shaped([row[2] for row in table]),
        "ci_lower": shaped([row[1] for row in table]),
        "ci_upper": shaped([row[3] for row in table]),
        "min": shaped([row[0] for row in table]),
        "max": shaped([row[4] for row in table]),
    }
```

Parameters:

| Name               | Type    | Description                                                 | Default    |
| ------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |

Returns:

| Type                  | Description                                            |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tuple[float, float]` | Lower and upper percentile points, on the 0-100 scale. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                          |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If confidence_level is not strictly between 0 and 1. |

Source code in `commol/api/inference/intervals.py`

```python
def ci_percentiles(confidence_level: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Lower and upper percentile points of a two-sided confidence interval.

    Parameters
    ----------
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[float, float]
        Lower and upper percentile points, on the 0-100 scale.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is not strictly between 0 and 1.
    """
    if not 0.0 < confidence_level < 1.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"confidence_level must be strictly between 0 and 1, got "
            f"{confidence_level}. Note this is a fraction, not a percentage: "
            f"use 0.95 for a 95% interval."
        )
    return (
        (1.0 - confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
        (1.0 + confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
    )
```

## registry

The runners of inference methods, looked up by configuration type.

A method registers its runner with `register`; `Calibrator.uncertainty`, `Calibrator.identifiability` and `SensitivityAnalysis.run` find it with `run_method`, and pass the runner themselves. The entry points know no method.

### Type Aliases

#### EntryPoint

```python
EntryPoint = Calibrator | SensitivityAnalysis
```

What a runner runs on: the calibrator of an uncertainty or identifiability method, or the analysis of a sensitivity method.

### Classes

### Functions:

#### register

Register the runner of an inference method.

Parameters:

| Name          | Type                     | Description                                           | Default                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| `runner`      | \`Callable\[\[Calibrator | SensitivityAnalysis, InferenceMethod\], BaseModel\]\` | Runs the method on the object of its entry point (a Calibrator, or a SensitivityAnalysis for a sensitivity method) and returns its result. |

| Type         | Description                       |

Source code in `commol/api/inference/registry.py`

```python
def register(
    method_type: type[MethodT],
    runner: Callable[[Any, MethodT], BaseModel],
) -> None:
    """
    Register the runner of an inference method.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method_type : type[InferenceMethod]
        The configuration type of the method.
    runner : Callable[[Calibrator | SensitivityAnalysis, InferenceMethod], BaseModel]
        Runs the method on the object of its entry point (a `Calibrator`,
        or a `SensitivityAnalysis` for a sensitivity method) and returns its
        result.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the type already has a runner.
    """
    if method_type in _RUNNERS:
        raise ValueError(f"{method_type.__name__} already has a runner.")
    _RUNNERS[method_type] = cast("Runner", runner)
```

```python
def registered() -> list[str]:
    """
    The names of the configuration types that have a runner.

    Returns
    -------
    list[str]
        Sorted names.
    """
    return sorted(method_type.__name__ for method_type in _RUNNERS)
```

#### run_method

```python
run_method(entry_point: EntryPoint, method: InferenceMethod[ResultT], kind: type[InferenceMethod[BaseModel]]) -> ResultT
```

Run `method` on `entry_point` with the runner of its type.

Parameters:

| Name          | Type                       | Description                                                                                              | Default                                               |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `entry_point` | \`Calibrator               | SensitivityAnalysis\`                                                                                    | The calibration problem, or the sensitivity analysis. |
| `method`      | `InferenceMethod[ResultT]` | The configuration of the method.                                                                         | *required*                                            |
| `kind`        | `type[InferenceMethod]`    | The kind of method the entry point takes: UncertaintyMethod, IdentifiabilityMethod or SensitivityMethod. | *required*                                            |

Returns:

| Type      | Description          |
| --------- | -------------------- |
| `ResultT` | The method's result. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `TypeError`  | If method is not of kind; the message names its entry point. |
| `ValueError` | If no runner is registered for the configuration's type.     |

Source code in `commol/api/inference/registry.py`

```python
def run_method(
    entry_point: EntryPoint,
    method: InferenceMethod[ResultT],
    kind: type[InferenceMethod[BaseModel]],
) -> ResultT:
    """
    Run `method` on `entry_point` with the runner of its type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    entry_point : Calibrator | SensitivityAnalysis
        The calibration problem, or the sensitivity analysis.
    method : InferenceMethod[ResultT]
        The configuration of the method.
    kind : type[InferenceMethod]
        The kind of method the entry point takes: `UncertaintyMethod`,
        `IdentifiabilityMethod` or `SensitivityMethod`.

    Returns
    -------
    ResultT
        The method's result.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If `method` is not of `kind`; the message names its entry point.
    ValueError
        If no runner is registered for the configuration's type.
    """
    if not isinstance(method, kind):
        right = next(
            (
                name
                for other, name in _ENTRY_POINTS.items()
                if isinstance(method, other)
            ),
            None,
        )
        hint = f" Run it with {right}." if right else ""
        raise TypeError(f"{type(method).__name__} is not a {kind.__name__}.{hint}")
    runner = _RUNNERS.get(type(method))
    if runner is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No method is registered for {type(method).__name__}. "
            f"Registered: {registered()}."
        )
    return cast("ResultT", runner(entry_point, method))
```

# Model Structure

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

A `Model` is a tree of Pydantic models. `ModelBuilder` creates it, `Model.to_json` writes it, and the Rust engine reads the same tree from JSON (`crates/commol-core/src/types/`). Most users never build these types by hand; read this page to understand model files or to work on Commol.

A model has a header, a **process** written once, a **structure** that lays the process out, and an **engine** that runs it. The process (bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions) is the same for every kind of model; the structure changes between kinds and is tagged in JSON by `kind`, and by `variant` for a narrower form of a structure. The kind today is `aggregate`: amounts per compartment.

```text
Model                      name, description, version, step_unit
├── parameters: [Parameter]                (a value may be a SeriesValue)
├── engine: ModelEngine
│   ├── type: "DifferenceEquations", "DifferentialEquations",
│   │         "StochasticEvents" or "StochasticSteps"
│   └── settings: ODESolver | StochasticEventsSettings | StochasticStepsSettings | None
│                                           (settings of that engine; None: its defaults)
├── process: Process
│   ├── bins: [Bin]
│   ├── accumulators: [Accumulator]
│   ├── stratifications: [Stratification]
│   │   └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
│   └── transitions: [Transition]          (impulse_at, impulse_every for impulses)
│       └── stratified_rates: [StratifiedRate]
│           └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
└── structure: Aggregate                   (kind: "aggregate", variant: None)
    ├── bin_amounts: {bin: amount | None}          (in the unit of the bin)
    ├── stratification_fractions: {stratification: {category: fraction}}
    ├── compartment_amounts: {compartment: amount}
    └── neighbors: Complete | Groups | None
```

In JSON the structure is an object with its `kind`, its `variant` and the fields of its class:

```json
{
  "name": "Model",
  "parameters": [],
  "engine": {"type": "DifferenceEquations", "settings": null},
  "process": {"bins": [], "accumulators": [], "stratifications": [], "transitions": []},
  "structure": {
    "kind": "aggregate",
    "variant": null,
    "bin_amounts": {"A": 990.0, "B": 10.0},
    "stratification_fractions": {},
    "compartment_amounts": {},
    "neighbors": null
  },
  "step_unit": null
}
```

`Model`, `Process`, `ModelStructure`, `Aggregate`, `Complete` and `Groups` are documented in [Model API](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/model/index.md). The engine must run the kind of the structure: a model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made, with an error that names the engine, both kinds and the engines of the kind of the model. A variant keeps the kind, the fields and the engines of its structure, and loads back as its own class ([Design decisions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/decisions/model-kinds/#a-model-is-a-header-a-process-a-structure-and-an-engine)).

## Bins and accumulators

## Bin

Bases: `BaseModel`

Defines a single bin (base category) of the process of a model.

A bin represents a fundamental category before stratification. The combination of a bin with all stratifications produces the actual compartments.

Source code in `commol/context/bin.py`

```python
class Bin(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a single bin (base category) of the process of a model.

    A bin represents a fundamental category before stratification. The combination
    of a bin with all stratifications produces the actual compartments.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier of the bin.
    name : str
        A descriptive, human-readable name for the bin.
    unit : str | None
        The unit of measurement for this bin.
        If None, the bin will use the model-level bin_unit when specified.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(..., description="Identifier of the bin.")
    name: str = Field(..., description="Descriptive, human-readable name for the bin.")
    unit: str | None = Field(
        None,
        description="Unit of measurement for this bin.",
    )

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.id)

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, Bin) and self.id == other.id
```

## Stratification

Bases: `BaseModel`

Defines a categorical subdivision of the compartments.

Attributes:

| Name          | Type                            | Description                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | `str`                           | Identifier of the stratification.                        |
| `categories`  | `list[str]`                     | List of the different stratification groups identifiers. |
| `description` | \`str                           | None\`                                                   |
| `conditions`  | \`list[StratificationCondition] | None\`                                                   |

Source code in `commol/context/stratification.py`

```python
class Stratification(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a categorical subdivision of the compartments.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier of the stratification.
    categories : list[str]
        List of the different stratification groups identifiers.
    description : str | None
        A human-readable description of the stratification.
    conditions : list[StratificationCondition] | None
        When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
        already-applied stratification categories satisfy ALL conditions.
        Compartments that do not satisfy the conditions are kept without
        appending this stratification's categories.

        May only reference stratifications declared before this one.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Identifier of the stratification.")
    categories: list[str] = Field(
        default=...,
        description="List of the different stratification groups identifiers.",
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the stratification."
    )
    conditions: list[StratificationCondition] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Conditions on previously-declared stratifications that must be "
            "satisfied for this stratification to expand a compartment."
        ),
    )

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.id)

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, Stratification) and self.id == other.id

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_length(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not empty.
        """
        if not self.categories:
            raise ValueError(
                (f"Stratification '{self.id}' must have at least one category.")
            )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_uniqueness(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not repeated.
        """
        categories_set = set(self.categories)

        if len(categories_set) != len(self.categories):
            duplicates = [
                item for item in categories_set if self.categories.count(item) > 1
            ]
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Categories for stratification '{self.id}' must not be repeated. "
                    f"Found duplicates: {list(set(duplicates))}."
                )
            )

        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_conditions_have_categories(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that stratification expansion conditions filter by category.
        """
        if self.conditions is None:
            return self

        for condition in self.conditions:
            if condition.category is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    (
                        f"Condition for stratification '{self.id}' referencing "
                        f"'{condition.stratification}' must include a category. "
                        "Category-less conditions are only valid for transition "
                        "target overrides."
                    )
                )

        return self
```

## StratificationCondition

Bases: `BaseModel`

Specifies a category within a stratification for rate matching.

When `to` is set, the matched category in the source compartment is replaced with the `to` category in the target compartment name. This enables cross-category transitions within the same bin (e.g., from `g1` to `g2`).

Attributes:

| Name             | Type  | Description                                                |
| ---------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stratification` | `str` | The ID of the stratification (e.g., "group", "type")       |
| `category`       | `str` | The category within that stratification (e.g., "g1", "t1") |
| `to`             | \`str | None\`                                                     |

Source code in `commol/context/stratification_condition.py`

```python
class StratificationCondition(BaseModel):
    """
    Specifies a category within a stratification for rate matching.

    When ``to`` is set, the matched category in the source compartment is
    replaced with the ``to`` category in the target compartment name. This
    enables cross-category transitions within the same bin (e.g., from ``g1``
    to ``g2``).

    Attributes
    ----------
    stratification : str
        The ID of the stratification (e.g., "group", "type")
    category : str
        The category within that stratification (e.g., "g1", "t1")
    to : str | None
        Target category override. When set, the target compartment will use
        this category instead of the source compartment's category for this
        stratification.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    stratification: str = Field(default=..., description="ID of the stratification")
    category: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Category within the stratification. When None, the condition acts as a "
            "target-only override: it does not filter source compartments but still "
            "contributes a 'to' category to the computed target compartment name."
        ),
    )
    to: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Target category override. When set, the target compartment uses "
            "this category instead of the source's for this stratification."
        ),
    )
```

## Parameter

Bases: `BaseModel`

Defines a global model parameter.

Attributes:

| Name          | Type    | Description                      |
| ------------- | ------- | -------------------------------- |

Source code in `commol/context/parameter.py`

```python
class Parameter(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a global model parameter.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        The identifier of the parameter.
    value : float | str | SeriesValue | None
        Value of the parameter. Can be:
        - float: A numerical constant value
        - str: A mathematical formula that can reference other parameters,
               special variables (total, total_<category>, step, t, pi, e), or contain
               mathematical expressions
        - SeriesValue: An empirical series evaluated via binary search
        - None: Indicates that the parameter needs to be calibrated before use
    description : str | None
        A human-readable description of the parameter.
    unit : str | None
        The unit of the parameter (e.g., "1/day", "dimensionless", "item").
        If None, the parameter has no unit specified.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Identifier of the parameter.")
    value: float | str | SeriesValue | None = Field(
        default=...,
        description=(
            "Value of the parameter. Can be a float (constant), "
            "str (formula), SeriesValue (empirical series), "
            "or None (requires calibration)."
        ),
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the parameter."
    )
    unit: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Unit of the parameter (e.g., '1/day', 'dimensionless', 'item').",
    )

    @field_validator("value")
    @classmethod
    def validate_value(
        cls, value: float | str | SeriesValue | None
    ) -> float | str | SeriesValue | None:
        """Validate the parameter value."""
        if value is None or isinstance(value, SeriesValue):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            return float(value)
        if not value.strip():
            raise ValueError("Formula cannot be empty")
        return value.strip()

    def is_calibrated(self) -> bool:
        """
        Check if the parameter has a value (is calibrated).

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            True if the parameter has a value, False if it needs calibration.
        """
        return self.value is not None

    def with_value(self, value: ParameterUpdate) -> "Parameter":
        """
        This parameter with another value.

        Parameters
        ----------
        value : ParameterUpdate
            The new value, as `Parameter.value` takes it. A list of
            (position, value) points replaces the points of a series and keeps
            its mode; a `SeriesValue` sets both.

        Returns
        -------
        Parameter
            A new parameter with the same id, description and unit.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``value`` is a list and this parameter is not a series, or
            ``value`` is not a valid value; the message names the parameter.
        """
        try:
            if isinstance(value, list):
                if not isinstance(self.value, SeriesValue):
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Parameter '{self.id}' is not a series, so a list of "
                        "points has no mode: pass a SeriesValue(data=..., mode=...)"
                    )
                value = SeriesValue(data=value, mode=self.value.mode)
            return Parameter(
                id=self.id, value=value, description=self.description, unit=self.unit
            )
        except ValidationError as error:
            reasons = "; ".join(detail["msg"] for detail in error.errors())
            raise ValueError(
                f"Parameter '{self.id}' cannot take {value!r}: {reasons}"
            ) from None
```

## Transition

Bases: `BaseModel`

Defines a rule for system evolution.

Attributes:

| Name               | Type                   | Description                   |
| ------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `id`               | `str`                  | Id of the transition.         |
| `source`           | `list[str]`            | The origin compartments.      |
| `target`           | `list[str]`            | The destination compartments. |
| `rate`             | \`str                  | None\`                        |
| `stratified_rates` | \`list[StratifiedRate] | None\`                        |

Source code in `commol/context/transition.py`

```python
class Transition(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a rule for system evolution.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Id of the transition.
    source : list[str]
        The origin compartments.
    target : list[str]
        The destination compartments.
    rate : str | None
        Default mathematical formula, parameter name, or constant value for the flow.
        Used when no stratified rate matches. Numeric values are automatically
        converted to strings during validation.

        Operators: +, -, *, /, % (modulo), ^ or ** (power)
        Functions: sin, cos, tan, exp, ln, sqrt, abs, min, max, if, etc.
        Constants: pi, e

        Note: Both ^ and ** are supported for exponentiation (** is converted to ^).

        Examples:
        - "k1" (parameter reference)
        - "0.5" (constant, can also be passed as float 0.5)
        - "k1 * A * B / total" (mathematical formula)
        - "0.3 * sin(2 * pi * t / 365)" (formula that changes along the axis)
        - "2^10" or "2**10" (power: both syntaxes work)
    stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRate] | None
        Stratification-specific rates. Each rate applies to compartments that match
        all specified stratification conditions.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Id of the transition.")
    source: list[str] = Field(default=..., description="Origin compartments.")
    target: list[str] = Field(default=..., description="Destination compartments.")
    accumulators: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Cumulative event counters incremented by this transition flow.",
    )

    rate: str | None = Field(
        None,
        description=(
            "Default rate expression (fallback when no stratified rate matches). "
            "Can be a parameter reference (e.g., 'k1'), a constant (e.g., '0.5'), "
            "or a mathematical expression (e.g., 'k1 * A * B / total'). "
            "Numeric values are automatically converted to strings during validation."
        ),
    )

    stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRate] | None = Field(
        default=None, description="List of stratification-specific rates"
    )

    per_compartment: bool | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "When True, the id of each source and target bin in a rate reads "
            "the compartment of each flow; any other bin keeps its total. A "
            "transition between categories ignores it."
        ),
    )

    impulse_at: list[float] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Positions on the axis where the transition is an impulse: at each "
            "one, the rate is a fraction (proportional) or an amount (absolute) "
            "moved at once. Between them the transition moves nothing."
        ),
    )

    impulse_every: tuple[float, float] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "(period, offset): the transition is an impulse at offset, "
            "offset + period, offset + 2 * period, ..."
        ),
    )

    @property
    def is_impulse(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the transition is an impulse rather than a continuous flow."""
        return self.impulse_at is not None or self.impulse_every is not None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_impulse(self) -> Self:
        """Check the impulse schedule: one kind, valid positions and period."""
        if self.impulse_at is not None and self.impulse_every is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Transition '{self.id}': set impulse_at or impulse_every, not both."
            )
        if self.impulse_at is not None:
            if not self.impulse_at:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': impulse_at needs at least one position."
                )
            bad = [p for p in self.impulse_at if not math.isfinite(p) or p < 0]
            if bad:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': impulse positions must be finite "
                    f"and not negative, got {bad}."
                )
        if self.impulse_every is not None:
            period, offset = self.impulse_every
            if not (math.isfinite(period) and period > 0):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': the impulse period must be "
                    f"positive, got {period}."
                )
            if not (math.isfinite(offset) and offset >= 0):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{self.id}': the impulse offset must be finite "
                    f"and not negative, got {offset}."
                )
        return self

    @field_validator("rate", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def validate_rate(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        """
        Convert numeric rates to strings and perform security and syntax validation.
        """
        if value is None:
            return value
        return _checked_rate(value)
```

## StratifiedRate

Bases: `BaseModel`

Defines a rate for specific stratification categories.

Source code in `commol/context/transition.py`

```python
class StratifiedRate(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a rate for specific stratification categories.

    Attributes
    ----------
    conditions : list[StratificationCondition]
        List of stratification-category pairs that must match
    rate : str
        Rate expression for compartments matching these conditions
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    conditions: list[StratificationCondition] = Field(
        default=..., description="Stratification conditions that must match"
    )
    rate: str = Field(
        default=..., description="Rate expression for matching compartments"
    )
    absolute: bool | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "When True, the flow is treated as absolute (not multiplied by the "
            "source amount). When None, inferred from whether the rate references "
            "any compartment variable."
        ),
    )

    @field_validator("conditions")
    @classmethod
    def validate_not_empty(
        cls, v: list[StratificationCondition]
    ) -> list[StratificationCondition]:
        """Ensure at least one stratification condition is specified."""
        if not v:
            raise ValueError(
                "conditions must contain at least one stratification condition"
            )
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_unique_stratifications(self) -> Self:
        """Ensure no duplicate stratification IDs."""
        strat_ids = [sc.stratification for sc in self.conditions]
        if len(strat_ids) != len(set(strat_ids)):
            duplicates = [s for s in strat_ids if strat_ids.count(s) > 1]
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Duplicate stratifications found: {list(set(duplicates))}. "
                    f"Each stratification can only be specified once per rate."
                )
            )
        return self

    @field_validator("rate", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def validate_rate(cls, value: str) -> str:
        """Perform security and syntax validation on the rate expression."""
        return _checked_rate(value)
```

## Engine

The engine's list of engines (`crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs`) validates the settings: settings of another engine raise an error that names both. `ODESolver` is documented in [Simulation API](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/simulation/index.md).

## ModelEngine

Bases: `BaseModel`

The engine that runs a model, and its settings.

Attributes:

| Name       | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`     | `str`            | Name of an engine of the engine's list, such as "DifferenceEquations" (discrete time) or "DifferentialEquations" (continuous time). The engine must run the kind of the structure of the model. |
| `settings` | \`EngineSettings | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Source code in `commol/context/engine.py`

```python
class ModelEngine(BaseModel):
    """
    The engine that runs a model, and its settings.

    Attributes
    ----------
    type : str
        Name of an engine of the engine's list, such as
        ``"DifferenceEquations"`` (discrete time) or
        ``"DifferentialEquations"`` (continuous time). The engine must run the
        kind of the structure of the model.
    settings : EngineSettings | None
        Settings of that engine; None uses its defaults.
        ``DifferentialEquations`` takes `ODESolver`, ``StochasticEvents``
        takes `StochasticEventsSettings` and ``StochasticSteps`` takes
        `StochasticStepsSettings`.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    type: str = Field(..., description="Name of the engine.")
    settings: EngineSettings | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Settings of the engine; None uses its defaults."
    )

    @field_validator("settings", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def settings_of_the_engine(cls, value: Any, info: ValidationInfo) -> Any:
        """Read settings given as a mapping with the class of their engine."""
        settings_class = _SETTINGS.get(info.data.get("type", ""))
        if isinstance(value, dict) and settings_class is not None:
            return settings_class.model_validate(value)
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_settings(self) -> Self:
        """Ask the engine's list whether it has the engine and the settings."""
        settings_json = (
            None if self.settings is None else self.settings.model_dump_json()
        )
        commol_rs.engine.EngineType(self.type).check_settings(settings_json)
        return self
```

## Initial conditions

`Aggregate` holds the fields and methods of `InitialConditions`, and checks them against the process when the model is built.

## InitialConditions

Bases: `BaseModel`

How much starts where: the amount of each bin and the split of it.

Every amount is in the unit of its bin, so bins of different units, such as people and a concentration, start without a total over them. `Aggregate` holds these fields and their methods; the checks against the bins and the stratifications of the process are in `Aggregate.check_model`.

Attributes:

| Name                       | Type                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bin_amounts`              | \`dict\[str, float            | None\]\`                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `stratification_fractions` | `dict[str, dict[str, float]]` | The fraction of each category, by stratification id and category: the split of the amount of every bin the stratification applies to. A conditional stratification splits only the group its conditions select. |
| `compartment_amounts`      | `dict[str, float]`            | Amounts of single expanded compartments, by compartment name, applied after the expansion.                                                                                                                      |

Source code in `commol/context/initial_conditions.py`

```python
class InitialConditions(BaseModel):
    """
    How much starts where: the amount of each bin and the split of it.

    Every amount is in the unit of its bin, so bins of different units, such
    as people and a concentration, start without a total over them.
    `Aggregate` holds these fields and their methods; the checks against the
    bins and the stratifications of the process are in
    `Aggregate.check_model`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    bin_amounts : dict[str, float | None]
        The amount of each bin at the start, by bin id, in the unit of the
        bin; finite and not negative. None leaves an amount for calibration.
    stratification_fractions : dict[str, dict[str, float]]
        The fraction of each category, by stratification id and category: the
        split of the amount of every bin the stratification applies to. A
        conditional stratification splits only the group its conditions
        select.
    compartment_amounts : dict[str, float]
        Amounts of single expanded compartments, by compartment name, applied
        after the expansion.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    bin_amounts: dict[str, float | None] = Field(
        ...,
        description=(
            "The amount of each bin, by bin id, in the unit of the bin. None "
            "leaves an amount for calibration."
        ),
    )
    stratification_fractions: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="The fraction of each category, by stratification id.",
    )
    compartment_amounts: dict[str, float] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "Amounts of single expanded compartments, applied after the expansion."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def reject_fractions_of_a_total(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        """Name the field of amounts that replaces a field of fractions.

        A total over bins of different units has no meaning, so the initial
        state is stated as amounts, and a structure with ``total``,
        ``bin_fractions`` or ``compartment_fractions`` is rejected with the
        field to use.
        """
        if isinstance(data, Mapping):
            stated = [field for field in _FRACTION_FIELDS if field in data]
            if stated:
                replacements = sorted({_FRACTION_FIELDS[field] for field in stated})
                raise ValueError(
                    f"An aggregate structure states the amount of each bin in "
                    f"the unit of the bin, not fractions of a total: replace "
                    f"{', '.join(stated)} with {' and '.join(replacements)}, "
                    f'such as bin_amounts={{"A": 990, "B": 10, "C": 0}}.'
                )
        return data

    @field_validator("bin_amounts")
    @classmethod
    def validate_bin_amounts(
        cls, value: dict[str, float | None]
    ) -> dict[str, float | None]:
        """Enforce that every bin amount is finite and not negative."""
        for bin_id, amount in value.items():
            if amount is not None:
                _check_amount(f"bin '{bin_id}'", amount)
        return value

    @field_validator("compartment_amounts")
    @classmethod
    def validate_compartment_amounts(cls, value: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Enforce that every compartment amount is finite and not negative."""
        for compartment, amount in value.items():
            _check_amount(f"compartment '{compartment}'", amount)
        return value

    def get_uncalibrated_bins(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Get list of bin IDs that have uncalibrated amounts (value = None).

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            List of bin IDs with uncalibrated initial conditions.
        """
        return [bin_id for bin_id, amount in self.bin_amounts.items() if amount is None]

    def get_categories_with_fractions(self) -> set[str]:
        """
        Get the categories that have a declared initial fraction.

        Returns
        -------
        set[str]
            Category names collected from ``stratification_fractions``. A
            category declared on a stratification but absent from the initial
            conditions is not included.
        """
        return {
            category
            for categories in self.stratification_fractions.values()
            for category in categories
        }

    def resolve_category(self, category: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Resolve a category id to its stratification and its bare name.

        A qualified id (``group:g1``) names the stratification. A bare name
        must be declared by exactly one stratification.

        Parameters
        ----------
        category : str
            A bare or qualified category id.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[str, str]
            The stratification id and the bare category name.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        stratification_id, separator, name = category.rpartition(CATEGORY_SEPARATOR)
        owners = [
            stratification
            for stratification, categories in self.stratification_fractions.items()
            if (not separator or stratification == stratification_id)
            and name in categories
        ]
        if len(owners) > 1:
            qualified = " or ".join(
                f"'{owner}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{name}'" for owner in owners
            )
            raise ValueError(
                f"Category '{category}' is ambiguous: it is declared by "
                f"stratifications {owners}. Qualify it as {qualified}."
            )
        if not owners:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Category '{category}' not found in initial conditions. "
                f"Available categories: {sorted(self.get_categories_with_fractions())}"
            )
        return owners[0], name

    def category_id(self, stratification: str, category: str) -> str:
        """
        Shortest id that names a category without ambiguity.

        Parameters
        ----------
        stratification : str
            Id of the stratification that declares the category.
        category : str
            Bare category name.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The bare name, or ``stratification:category`` when another
            stratification declares a category of the same name.
        """
        declaring = sum(
            category in categories
            for categories in self.stratification_fractions.values()
        )
        if declaring > 1:
            return f"{stratification}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{category}"
        return category

    def get_category_fraction(self, category: str) -> float:
        """
        Get the fraction of a category within the group it subdivides.

        Parameters
        ----------
        category : str
            A category id, bare or qualified (``group:g1``).

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The declared fraction, relative to the group the category's
            stratification applies to rather than to the whole model.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        stratification, name = self.resolve_category(category)
        return self.stratification_fractions[stratification][name]

    def _apply_stratification_update(
        self, stratification: str, named: Mapping[str, float]
    ) -> None:
        """Write the fractions of a single stratification."""
        categories = self.stratification_fractions[stratification]
        unnamed = [category for category in categories if category not in named]
        total = sum(named.values())

        if len(unnamed) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot update stratification '{stratification}': "
                f"categories {sorted(unnamed)} were left unnamed. At most one "
                f"category may be omitted, so that it can take the remaining "
                f"fraction."
            )
        if not unnamed and not math.isclose(total, 1.0, abs_tol=1e-6):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Fractions for stratification '{stratification}' "
                f"must sum to 1.0, got {total:.6f}. Values: {dict(named)}"
            )
        if unnamed and total > 1.0 + 1e-6:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Fractions for stratification '{stratification}' "
                f"sum to {total:.6f}, which would leave a negative fraction for "
                f"'{unnamed[0]}'. Values: {dict(named)}"
            )

        remainder = max(0.0, 1.0 - total)
        for category in categories:
            categories[category] = named.get(category, remainder)

    def update_stratification_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Update stratification category fractions by category name.

        Categories belonging to several stratifications may be given in one
        call. A category name declared by more than one stratification must be
        qualified with its stratification, as in ``group:g1``. Within each
        stratification, at most one category may be omitted; the omitted
        category receives the remaining fraction so that the stratification
        sums to 1.0. When every category is given, the values
        must already sum to 1.0.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fractions : Mapping[str, float]
            Dictionary mapping category names, bare or qualified, to their new
            fraction values. Each value must lie between 0.0 and 1.0.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a category is not found or is ambiguous, a value lies outside
            [0.0, 1.0], a stratification has more than one category omitted,
            fully specified values do not sum to 1.0, or the given values
            exceed 1.0.
        """
        for category, value in fractions.items():
            _check_fraction(f"category '{category}'", value)

        by_stratification: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
        for category, value in fractions.items():
            stratification, name = self.resolve_category(category)
            by_stratification.setdefault(stratification, {})[name] = value

        for stratification, named in by_stratification.items():
            self._apply_stratification_update(stratification, named)

    def _upsert_compartment_amounts(self, amounts: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Upsert per-compartment overrides by expanded compartment name.

        A compartment already present in ``compartment_amounts`` has its
        amount replaced; a new one is appended. Compartment names depend on
        the expansion of the process, so
        :meth:`~commol.context.aggregate.Aggregate.update_compartment_amounts`
        validates them against the engine, not here.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an amount is not finite or is negative.
        """
        for compartment, amount in amounts.items():
            _check_amount(f"compartment '{compartment}'", amount)
        self.compartment_amounts.update(amounts)

    def update_bin_amounts(self, amounts: Mapping[str, float | None]) -> None:
        """
        Update bin amounts by bin ID.

        Every amount is checked before any bin changes, so a rejected call
        leaves the initial conditions unchanged. The bins of one unit keep no
        sum: to move an amount between bins, update every bin involved.

        Parameters
        ----------
        amounts : Mapping[str, float | None]
            Dictionary mapping bin IDs to their new amount, in the unit of the
            bin. None marks a bin that needs calibration.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a bin ID is not found in the initial conditions, or an amount
            is not finite or is negative.
        """
        unknown = sorted(set(amounts) - set(self.bin_amounts))
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Bin(s) {unknown} not found in initial conditions. "
                f"Available bins: {list(self.bin_amounts)}"
            )
        for bin_id, amount in amounts.items():
            if amount is not None:
                _check_amount(f"bin '{bin_id}'", amount)
        self.bin_amounts.update(amounts)
```

### Methods:

#### reject_fractions_of_a_total

```python
reject_fractions_of_a_total(data: Any) -> Any
```

Name the field of amounts that replaces a field of fractions.

A total over bins of different units has no meaning, so the initial state is stated as amounts, and a structure with `total`, `bin_fractions` or `compartment_fractions` is rejected with the field to use.

Source code in `commol/context/initial_conditions.py`

```python
@model_validator(mode="before")
@classmethod
def reject_fractions_of_a_total(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
    """Name the field of amounts that replaces a field of fractions.

    A total over bins of different units has no meaning, so the initial
    state is stated as amounts, and a structure with ``total``,
    ``bin_fractions`` or ``compartment_fractions`` is rejected with the
    field to use.
    """
    if isinstance(data, Mapping):
        stated = [field for field in _FRACTION_FIELDS if field in data]
        if stated:
            replacements = sorted({_FRACTION_FIELDS[field] for field in stated})
            raise ValueError(
                f"An aggregate structure states the amount of each bin in "
                f"the unit of the bin, not fractions of a total: replace "
                f"{', '.join(stated)} with {' and '.join(replacements)}, "
                f'such as bin_amounts={{"A": 990, "B": 10, "C": 0}}.'
            )
    return data
```

#### validate_bin_amounts

```python
validate_bin_amounts(value: dict[str, float | None]) -> dict[str, float | None]
```

Enforce that every bin amount is finite and not negative.

Source code in `commol/context/initial_conditions.py`

```python
@field_validator("bin_amounts")
@classmethod
def validate_bin_amounts(
    cls, value: dict[str, float | None]
) -> dict[str, float | None]:
    """Enforce that every bin amount is finite and not negative."""
    for bin_id, amount in value.items():
        if amount is not None:
            _check_amount(f"bin '{bin_id}'", amount)
    return value
```

```python
def get_categories_with_fractions(self) -> set[str]:
    """
    Get the categories that have a declared initial fraction.

    Returns
    -------
    set[str]
        Category names collected from ``stratification_fractions``. A
        category declared on a stratification but absent from the initial
        conditions is not included.
    """
    return {
        category
        for categories in self.stratification_fractions.values()
        for category in categories
    }
```

```python
def resolve_category(self, category: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """
    Resolve a category id to its stratification and its bare name.

    A qualified id (``group:g1``) names the stratification. A bare name
    must be declared by exactly one stratification.

    Parameters
    ----------
    category : str
        A bare or qualified category id.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[str, str]
        The stratification id and the bare category name.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
    """
    stratification_id, separator, name = category.rpartition(CATEGORY_SEPARATOR)
    owners = [
        stratification
        for stratification, categories in self.stratification_fractions.items()
        if (not separator or stratification == stratification_id)
        and name in categories
    ]

        qualified = " or ".join(
            f"'{owner}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{name}'" for owner in owners
        )

            f"stratifications {owners}. Qualify it as {qualified}."
        )

            f"Category '{category}' not found in initial conditions. "
            f"Available categories: {sorted(self.get_categories_with_fractions())}"
```
